mission.name: The Half-Open Door
mission.description: Harborline Logistics gave its finance dashboard a dedicated IAM user, ledgerlens-report. The dashboard can see the file list of the harborline-reports bucket, but every attempt to open or download a report fails with AccessDenied. The user has a single inline policy called report-access, and the finance team is waiting on the Q3 numbers.
mission.objective: Let ledgerlens-report download objects from the reports/ folder of harborline-reports. The dashboard must stay read-only and must not be able to reach any other bucket.

mission.name: Wrong Side of the Law
mission.description: PixelForge's image-upload worker runs as the IAM role pixelforge-uploader. Since this morning's "permissions cleanup" every upload fails with AccessDenied, and the support queue is filling up. The worker can still list the bucket, so the role itself is fine — something in its inline policy is actively blocking writes.
mission.objective: Make the role pixelforge-uploader able to upload objects under s3://pixelforge-uploads/incoming/ — without giving it write access to any other bucket or prefix.

mission.name: Fat Fingers
mission.description: Lantern Studio resizes customer photos with a small worker that runs as the IAM user lantern-thumbs. It reads originals from lantern-originals and writes the resized copies to lantern-thumbnails. A teammate rewrote its inline policy by hand last night; this morning both halves of the job fail with AccessDenied even though the policy "looks right" in code review.
mission.objective: Get lantern-thumbs working again: it must be able to read objects from lantern-originals and write objects to lantern-thumbnails, and nothing more than that.

mission.name: Right Queue, Wrong Address
mission.description: Tidewater Freight's order consumer runs as the IAM user orderflow-consumer. It pulls orders from the SQS queue orders-prod and parks poison messages in orders-dlq. After the policy was moved over from the staging account the consumer sees AccessDenied on both queues, although the queue names in the policy are spelled correctly.
mission.objective: Make orderflow-consumer able to receive and delete messages on orders-prod and to send messages to orders-dlq. It must not be able to touch either queue in any other way.

mission.name: The Bare Role
mission.description: Bluefin Payments has a Lambda function, invoice-digest, that reads the day's invoice files from the bucket bluefin-invoices and writes a summary file into bluefin-digests. It was deployed this morning with a freshly created execution role, invoice-digest-role, and ever since the function returns an error instead of a digest. The role's trust policy is correct; someone just never gave it any permissions.
mission.objective: Give invoice-digest-role exactly the S3 access invoice-digest needs (read invoices, write digests) so the function runs successfully, without opening other buckets.

mission.name: Trust Issues
mission.description: Orbit Ledger recently consolidated its AWS accounts. The nightly bookkeeping batch signs in as the IAM user ledger-batch and is supposed to assume the role ledger-nightly to read the books in the orbit-ledger-books bucket. Since the migration, assuming the role fails with AccessDenied, even though ledger-batch is allowed to call sts:AssumeRole on it.
mission.objective: Let ledger-batch assume ledger-nightly and read the books. Other IAM users in the account that are allowed to call sts:AssumeRole in general must still be unable to assume this role.

mission.name: Cloned Credentials
mission.description: Quayside Gaming keeps a break-glass role, sre-breakglass, that the on-call engineer (IAM user sre-oncall) assumes to purge the stuck payments-retry queue during incidents. The role was made by cloning the trust policy of an EC2 instance role to save time. During tonight's incident the on-call engineer could not assume it at all.
mission.objective: Let sre-oncall assume sre-breakglass and purge the payments-retry queue. The second IAM user, sre-intern, may call sts:AssumeRole in general but must not be able to use this role.

mission.name: Dropped Baton
mission.description: Kestrel Retail's release pipeline runs as the IAM user kestrel-releaser. It may create Lambda functions named kestrel-*, and the execution role promo-fn-role already exists for them. Yet every deployment dies with AccessDenied the moment the pipeline tries to attach the role to the new function. There is also a powerful role, platform-admin-role, in the account that no pipeline should ever be able to hand to a function.
mission.objective: Let kestrel-releaser create Lambda functions that use promo-fn-role, while it remains unable to create functions that use platform-admin-role.

mission.name: First Day, No Access
mission.description: Nimbus Analytics hired Priya Nair today. Her IAM user, nimbus-priya, was created and she can sign in, but every call she makes, including listing the curated data lake bucket, comes back AccessDenied. At Nimbus nobody has permissions attached to their own user; access is handed out through groups, and there are several groups in the account for different kinds of people.
mission.objective: Give nimbus-priya the access of a regular data analyst: she must be able to read from the curated data lake bucket. She is not a platform administrator and not a contractor, so she must not read the raw landing bucket or manage IAM. Do not attach policies directly to her user.

mission.name: The Empty Club
mission.description: The Pigeonpost helpdesk keeps customer screenshots in the S3 bucket ticket-attachments. Agents Dana and Omar are members of the IAM group helpdesk-agents, but neither can upload or open an attachment: every call gets AccessDenied. Somebody created the group last week and never gave it any permissions. Three customer-managed policies for this bucket already exist in the account, written by the security team.
mission.objective: Make every member of helpdesk-agents able to upload and download ticket attachments, but not delete them. Fix it at group level so that future agents get the same access just by joining.

mission.name: Data Stays in Europe
mission.description: Meridian Health must keep patient events inside the EU. Its EU ingest worker (IAM user meridian-eu-worker) is only supposed to touch SQS queues through eu-west-1, so the security team wrote a policy that allows SQS actions when the request goes to that region. After the policy was rolled out the worker cannot use the eu-west-1 queue either. The Condition block was written by hand from memory.
mission.objective: Let meridian-eu-worker send and receive messages on the eu-west-1 queue patient-events-eu, while keeping the residency guardrail: it must still be refused when it calls SQS in us-east-1.

mission.name: Almost, But Not Quite
mission.description: Ashgrove Law lets its case clerk (IAM user ashgrove-clerk) browse only the 2025 matters in the case-files bucket. The policy allows ListBucket when the requested prefix lies under matters/2025/, and the author is certain it is correct: the value even contains the right wildcard. Yet the clerk cannot list matters/2025/ or any folder below it.
mission.objective: Let ashgrove-clerk list matters/2025/ and every folder below it, and read the files there. Browsing any other part of the bucket, including matters/2024/ and the bucket root, must stay forbidden.

mission.name: Dollar Signs Without Meaning
mission.description: Lumen Studios gives every employee a private folder in the lumen-homes bucket, named after their IAM user. One shared policy, home-folders, is meant to resolve ${aws:username} to each person's own folder. It is attached to the group lumen-staff, which both Alice and Bob belong to. Neither can open a single file in their own folder, and the policy document looks just like the examples in the docs.
mission.objective: Make home-folders work for everyone in lumen-staff: each user can read and write files under their own folder (a prefix named after their username) in lumen-homes, and cannot read anybody else's. Keep using the one shared managed policy.

mission.name: Frozen in Time
mission.description: Forgepoint Software deploys build artifacts with the IAM user forge-deployer. The user has the AWS managed policy AmazonS3FullAccess, so S3 should not be a problem, but uploads and deletes in the artifacts bucket now fail with AccessDenied. Over the years the user collected a few inline policies: some from past incidents, one that protects the production ledger bucket on purpose, and the ledger bucket must stay write-protected.
mission.objective: Restore forge-deployer's ability to upload and delete objects in forge-artifacts. Keep the intentional protection on forge-ledger-prod: the user must still be unable to write to it. Do not remove the managed policy.

mission.name: One Hat Short
mission.description: Cobalt Bank's external auditor signs in as the IAM user cobalt-auditor and is meant to switch into the role cobalt-audit-readonly to read the cobalt-audit-logs bucket. The role's trust policy already trusts the account, and the auditor has been told the role ARN, but "aws sts assume-role" is answered with AccessDenied. There is a second role in the account, cobalt-finance-admin, with the same trust policy and far more power.
mission.objective: Let cobalt-auditor assume cobalt-audit-readonly and read the audit logs through it. The auditor must still be unable to assume cobalt-finance-admin.
concepts: identity-based permission to assume a role

mission.name: The Secret Handshake
mission.description: Northwind Grocers lets the monitoring vendor MetricWave read its metrics export bucket (northwind-metrics-export). MetricWave's service signs in as the IAM user metricwave-svc and assumes the role metricwave-reader. Because the vendor serves many customers, the role's trust policy demands a shared external ID. MetricWave's onboarding sheet says their agent sends the external ID "mw-5d1f-prod-8841". Since go-live every assume-role call from the vendor is refused.
mission.objective: Make metricwave-svc able to assume metricwave-reader with the external ID from the vendor's onboarding sheet and read the export. Calls without an external ID, or with a different one, must still be refused.

mission.name: The Invisible Ceiling
mission.description: Skyhook Robotics onboarded an intern, skyhook-intern, and the team lead gave the user a broad S3 identity policy so nobody has to keep adjusting it. The platform team added a permission boundary, intern-boundary, as a safety net. The intern's first task is to upload test recordings into the sandbox bucket skyhook-sandbox-recordings, and every upload fails with AccessDenied. The identity policy was checked three times and clearly allows s3 actions.
mission.objective: Let skyhook-intern upload to skyhook-sandbox-recordings while the intern stays boxed in: no write access to skyhook-prod-telemetry, and the boundary must stay attached to the user.

mission.name: Scope Creep
mission.description: Vantage Media's render farm worker runs as the IAM user vantage-render. Its policy reads source files from vantage-assets (and its EU twin vantage-assets-eu) and writes finished videos to vantage-renders. To "save typing" someone wrote the bucket ARNs as vantage-*. Everything works, which is exactly why nobody noticed that a security scan just flagged the worker as able to read other buckets in the account.
mission.objective: Tighten vantage-render's policy so it can still read the two asset buckets and write to vantage-renders, but can no longer touch any other bucket whose name starts with vantage-.

mission.name: Lost in the Path
mission.description: Redwood Labs lets its contractors manage their own credentials. The IAM group redwood-contractors carries a self-service policy: each member may list and inspect their own access keys, using the policy variable for the caller's username so one policy fits everyone. All contractor accounts live under the IAM path /contractors/. Nobody can use the self-service policy; every attempt to list their own keys gets AccessDenied, while the identical policy worked in the pilot with a few test accounts.
mission.objective: Make each member of redwood-contractors able to list and inspect their own access keys, and only their own. Other contractors' keys and other IAM users' keys must remain off limits.

mission.name: The Bloated Policy
mission.description: Fleetwise Telematics collects vehicle telemetry in one S3 bucket per region, fleet-<region>-telemetry, fourteen in total. The analytics user fleet-ops is supposed to read from all of them. A generated policy draft is sitting in your workspace, but whenever someone tries to attach it to the user, IAM refuses it. For now fleet-ops can only list bucket names. There is also a fleet-payroll bucket in the account that the analytics user must never read.
mission.objective: Give fleet-ops read access (list and get) to all fourteen regional telemetry buckets, without exposing fleet-payroll, even though the draft cannot be attached the way it is.

mission.name: Guest List Gone Wrong
mission.description: Harbor Print shares customer proofs with a partner studio through the S3 bucket harborprint-proofs. The partner's reviewer signs in as the IAM user proofreader, which has no IAM permissions of its own: access is granted by the bucket policy, which was rewritten by hand yesterday. Today the reviewer can neither list the bucket nor open a proof. A second partner account, proof-intern, must stay locked out of the bucket.
mission.objective: Repair the bucket policy so that proofreader can list the bucket and download proofs from proofs/. Nobody else, including proof-intern, may gain access, and the reviewer must not be able to upload or delete.

mission.name: Manifest Not Found
mission.description: Harborline Freight's dock scanners push container manifests through a small ingest service that runs as the IAM user ingest-bot. After last night's region migration the service restarts in a loop and the log is full of NoSuchBucket errors. The service configuration is in ingest.env in your workspace. Somebody mentioned that a bucket "with almost the same name" was created during the migration.
mission.objective: Make the manifest bucket that the ingest service is configured to use available, so ingest-bot can store a manifest in it and read it back.

mission.name: Keep Out
mission.description: Meridian Insurance keeps its quarterly audit packs in the bucket meridian-audit-reports. The external auditor logs in as the IAM user auditor-dana, and since Monday every download fails with AccessDenied. Dana's user has no IAM permissions of its own: access was always granted by the bucket policy, a copy of which is in your workspace. The same bucket also holds payroll exports that Dana must never see.
mission.objective: Let auditor-dana download everything under reports/ in meridian-audit-reports, while payroll/ stays off limits, nobody gains write access, and other users (such as intern-lee) still get nothing.

mission.name: Read-Only Trap
mission.description: Nimbus Labs' CI pipeline authenticates as the IAM user ci-runner. It can pull yesterday's build from the bucket nimbus-build-artifacts without trouble, but every publish step fails with AccessDenied. Release engineering says the bucket policy (copy in your workspace) "definitely has a publish statement". The release-manager user publishes to releases/ and must keep doing so.
mission.objective: Let ci-runner upload build outputs under artifacts/ in nimbus-build-artifacts while it keeps reading the bucket. It must not be able to write anywhere else or delete anything, and release-manager must still be able to publish under releases/.

mission.name: Lost History
mission.description: Ledgerly stores customer contracts in the bucket ledgerly-contracts and the contract service (IAM user contract-svc) saves revisions by uploading to the same key again. Yesterday a paralegal's second upload silently replaced the signed Orbit master agreement, and nobody can get the original back. The service's code already asks S3 for older revisions, but there are none to return.
mission.objective: Make ledgerly-contracts keep every revision of a contract, so that when contract-svc uploads the same key twice, both revisions can be listed and the older one can be downloaded again.

mission.name: Suspended Animation
mission.description: PixelCart's storefront reads its feature switches from flags.json in the bucket pixelcart-feature-flags, written by the IAM user flag-publisher. Last week someone paused versioning "to save storage costs" and a botched deploy then overwrote flags.json with garbage. The checkout page is broken, and the team cannot see why uploads no longer produce separate revisions. The last good flags were published a few days earlier.
mission.objective: Bring back the last good flags.json (the version that has "rollout": 50) as the live object, and make the bucket keep a separate, retrievable version for every future upload.

mission.name: The Force Field
mission.description: Lumen Design publishes its logos and press kit from the bucket lumen-brand-assets. The marketing intern wrote a public-read policy (public-read-policy.json in your workspace) and applied it, but the command fails with Access Denied even for the account owner, and the press page shows broken images. Security hardened this bucket last quarter and nobody wrote down how. The bucket also holds unreleased contract drafts that must stay private.
mission.objective: Publish the press kit so that anyone can download objects under public/ in lumen-brand-assets, while private/ stays unreadable to everyone but the owner. Do not strip the other protections from the bucket: new public ACLs must remain blocked.

mission.name: The CORS Complaint
mission.description: Tidewater Logistics' shipment dashboard, served from https://dashboard.tidewater.example, lets staff drag proof-of-delivery photos straight into the bucket tidewater-pod-photos and then displays them. Uploads die in the browser with "blocked by CORS policy: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header", although the same requests work from curl. The frontend sends a Content-Type header on its PUT requests and reads the ETag response header to confirm each upload.
mission.objective: Make the browser preflight succeed for the dashboard origin so it can GET and PUT objects with a Content-Type header and read ETag from responses. Other origins must stay blocked, and the dashboard must not get methods it does not use (it never deletes).

mission.name: Wrong Domain Allowed
mission.description: BrightCart serves product media from the bucket brightcart-media. The storefront (https://shop.brightcart.example) loads images fine, but the staff admin app at https://admin.brightcart.example cannot upload or delete media: the browser reports a CORS error on the preflight. A previous engineer already added CORS rules for both apps, saved in cors.json in your workspace, and swears they match. The admin app uploads with PUT and removes media with DELETE, sending Content-Type headers.
mission.objective: Fix the CORS configuration so the admin app can PUT and DELETE media while the storefront keeps working exactly as before (read-only). No other website may be allowed, including look-alike domains.

mission.name: Eternal Storage
mission.description: Ember Games ships application logs to the bucket ember-app-logs, and the storage bill has doubled since spring. Finance points out that the lifecycle rules "expire-debug-logs" and "expire-error-logs" are enabled, yet October's debug logs are still there. The rules are saved as lifecycle.json in your workspace. Careful: the audit logs under app-logs/audit/ are retained for legal reasons and must never expire.
mission.objective: Make the debug logs expire after at most 14 days, keep the error logs expiring after at most 90 days, and ensure the audit logs are not covered by any expiration rule.

mission.name: Incomplete Uploads Pile Up
mission.description: DataVault's nightly export job uploads multi-gigabyte files to the bucket datavault-exports using multipart upload. When the job's pods get evicted, the half-finished uploads are never completed or aborted, and their stored parts are billed forever. Finance found several of them listed in the bucket. The bucket already has a lifecycle rule that moves old exports to cheaper storage (saved as lifecycle.json in your workspace), which the team wants to keep as it is.
mission.objective: Stop abandoned multipart uploads from accumulating anywhere in the bucket by having them aborted automatically after at most 7 days, keep the existing storage-class transition rule working, and clean up the incomplete uploads that are there right now.

mission.name: Silent Arrivals
mission.description: AcornPay's accounts-payable robot is supposed to wake up whenever a supplier invoice PDF lands in s3://acornpay-invoices/inbox/. It reads jobs from the SQS queue invoice-intake. Since the bucket was rebuilt last week the queue stays empty: scanner-svc uploads invoices fine, but the robot never hears about them. Other file types in inbox/ (cover letters, notes) and anything outside inbox/ must not create jobs.
mission.objective: Make S3 send a message to the queue invoice-intake whenever a new .pdf object is created under inbox/, and only then.

mission.name: Wrong Trigger
mission.description: SnapFolio's photo gallery should generate a thumbnail for every image that is uploaded to uploads/ in the bucket snapfolio-gallery. The worker reads jobs from the queue thumbnail-jobs. Since the release it only fires when someone deletes a photo, and the gallery fills with grey placeholders. The bucket's notification setup (saved as notification.json in your workspace) also feeds the queue deletion-audit, which compliance uses to record deletions of customer originals under originals/. That audit trail is working and must not change.
mission.objective: Make new objects under uploads/ trigger the thumbnail-jobs queue (and uploads to uploads/ only), without disturbing the deletion audit of originals/.

mission.name: Plaintext Exposure
mission.description: Riverside Imaging stores patient scans in the bucket riverside-scans. An internal audit found the bucket has no default encryption, so scans are written as plain objects. The compliance policy requires server-side encryption with the clinic's own customer managed KMS key (alias alias/riverside-phi), not S3-managed keys and not the AWS managed key. The billing team has a second CMK, alias/riverside-billing, which must not be used here. The bucket already contains one scan that was uploaded before the audit.
mission.objective: Configure default encryption on riverside-scans with SSE-KMS using the alias/riverside-phi key (with S3 Bucket Keys enabled to cut KMS request cost), and re-encrypt the existing scan under scans/ with the same key.

mission.name: The Broken Gate
mission.description: Quillhouse Press exchanges files with a printing partner through the bucket quillhouse-partner-drop. The partner's service user partner-sync must list and download from outbound/ and upload to inbound/. Nothing else. The bucket policy was reviewed by a linter and "looks perfectly valid" (it is in your workspace as bucket-policy.json), yet the partner reports that listing, downloading and uploading all fail with AccessDenied. The press's own catalogue under internal/ must stay invisible to the partner.
mission.objective: Repair the bucket policy so partner-sync can list outbound/ and inbound/, download from outbound/, and upload to inbound/, while it still cannot read internal/, write to outbound/, delete anything, or list the bucket without a prefix. Other users must get nothing.

mission.name: Public by Accident
mission.description: Sunrise Studio shares wedding galleries from the bucket sunrise-photos. A security scan flagged it: the bucket ACL grants READ to the AllUsers group, and the two gallery photos carry public-read ACLs of their own, left over from an old uploader script. The web app (IAM user renderer-app) reads the photos through its own IAM permissions, never through ACLs. The bucket still allows ACLs, which is how the script got away with it.
mission.objective: Remove every public ACL grant from the bucket and from the existing objects without deleting any photo, make sure ACLs cannot expose the bucket again, and keep renderer-app able to read the galleries.

mission.name: Silent Website
mission.description: Driftwood Software's documentation site is a set of static files in the bucket driftwood-docs-site (index.html, a guides/ section with its own index.html, a branded 404.html). Tonight's launch announcement went out and every visit to the website endpoint shows an XML error page instead of the site. Nobody remembers enabling website hosting on this bucket in the first place. An old error.html from the previous site design is still in the bucket.
mission.objective: Serve the files as a website: the root and every folder (such as /guides/) must show their index.html, and mistyped URLs must show the site's own 404.html page with a 404 status.

mission.name: No Paper Trail
mission.description: Corvid Retail's incident response team asked who downloaded the leaked price list from the bucket corvid-storefront-assets last Tuesday. Nobody can tell: server access logging was never turned on and no log bucket exists. Security wants the logs delivered into a dedicated bucket named corvid-access-logs under the prefix storefront/. A logging bucket used to be set up by a Terraform module that has since been retired, and the new bucket will need to let the S3 logging service write into it.
mission.objective: Turn on server access logging for corvid-storefront-assets with delivery to corvid-access-logs under storefront/, and give the S3 logging service (and only that service) permission to write the log files there.

mission.name: Too Flexible
mission.description: Fennel Capital keeps its audited general ledgers in the bucket fennel-ledger-archive, which has Object Lock enabled. The regulator's examination found that a privileged administrator could still shorten or lift the retention, because everything was written in GOVERNANCE mode with only a 30 day default. Rules require that ledger records are immutable for 7 years, with no one able to bypass that, not even the root user. Three ledger versions are stored today under ledger/ (two versions of 2025 and the 2024 file), each locked in GOVERNANCE until 2028-01-01.
mission.objective: Make every stored version under ledger/ immutable in COMPLIANCE mode (keeping at least the current 2028-01-01 retain-until date), and change the bucket's default so that every future object is locked in COMPLIANCE mode for at least 7 years.

mission.name: Expensive Archive
mission.description: Hotline Media's web team reports that the autumn campaign banner and the site stylesheet in the bucket hotline-media load for hours, or not at all: both objects under live/ are stored in the GLACIER class. Someone wrote a lifecycle rule "age-out-media" meant for old campaigns, but it names the wrong prefix, so it keeps pushing live files into Glacier a day after they are touched. The lifecycle rule for old campaigns under archive/ is correct and those objects belong in Glacier. The live objects carry a Content-Type and custom metadata that the site depends on.
mission.objective: Put the objects under live/ back in the STANDARD storage class without losing their content, Content-Type or user metadata, stop the lifecycle from archiving them again, and leave the archive/ objects and their rule alone.

mission.name: Unexpected Bills
mission.description: Ridgeline Analytics' finance team is fielding angry mail: partner companies say their automated downloads from the Ridgeline buckets now fail or show up on their own AWS invoice. Requester Pays was switched on across the account last week by a script that was supposed to touch only the public dataset bucket ridgeline-open-data, where downloaders really are meant to pay for their own transfer. All other Ridgeline buckets are normal buckets that the company pays for.
mission.objective: Find every Ridgeline bucket that has Requester Pays turned on by mistake and make the bucket owner pay again, but leave the public dataset bucket ridgeline-open-data on Requester Pays.

mission.name: Return to Sender
mission.description: Cobalt Parcel prints its shipping labels with a small Lambda function that the nightly dispatch job calls by the name parcel-label-formatter. Last night the job died on its first call and the warehouse printed zero labels. The platform team says the function "must have been cleaned up with the old sandbox", but the IAM role it ran under is still there, and the source code is sitting in your workspace.
mission.objective: Make parcel-label-formatter callable again, running the code from your workspace under the existing label role, so that the dispatch job gets correctly formatted labels back.

mission.name: End of the Line
mission.description: Harborline Ledger's month-end close runs through the Lambda function ledger-month-close. This morning finance reported that the close job produces no totals at all. The function was deployed years ago and nobody has touched its code; the platform team only mentions that "the runtime team sent a deprecation email some time ago".
mission.objective: Get ledger-month-close producing totals again without rewriting its source code: it must run on a Python runtime that Lambda still supports and that actually understands the code.

mission.name: Wrong Door, Right House
mission.description: Pinecrest Outfitters pushes every new order to its dropshipping partners through a small Node.js Lambda called webhook-relay. Since the migration to the new deployment pipeline, partners report that no order webhooks arrive. The function's package was uploaded correctly and its source is in your workspace, yet every invocation dies immediately.
mission.objective: Make webhook-relay sign and relay order events again. The deployed package must stay as it is; fix how Lambda is told to find the entry point.

mission.name: Nobody Home
mission.description: Tidewater Insurance archives every claim receipt through the Lambda function claim-receipt-archiver. Last week the platform team ran an "unused IAM roles" cleanup. Since then the security team's nightly audit flags the function: the role in its configuration no longer exists. Whoever recreates it has to be careful, because the legal-hold bucket tidewater-claim-evidence sits in the same account and the archiver's event accepts a bucket override.
mission.objective: Give claim-receipt-archiver a working execution role that trusts Lambda and lets it write receipts to tidewater-claim-receipts and its own logs, but not to any other bucket.

mission.name: Borrowed Badge
mission.description: Lumen Photo Co's thumbnail scanner function was moved onto a role that was originally written for the render farm's EC2 box. A new security scanner now flags the role as "cannot be assumed by the service that uses it", and the platform lead wants it fixed before the audit on Friday. The CI user also assumes this role for dry-runs and must keep doing so, and the role's permissions have been hand-tuned over a year, so nobody wants to recreate it.
mission.objective: Make the role lumen-thumb-scanner assumable by the Lambda service, remove the EC2 service from its trust, and keep the CI deployer's access and the role's existing permissions intact.

mission.name: The Blank Config
mission.description: Maple Treasury's invoicing service converts foreign-currency invoices through a Lambda function called fx-rate-lookup. After a re-deploy the function crashes on every call with a KeyError, and invoices are piling up unpriced. The code is unchanged and was written to read its settings from environment variables, one of which still has to be provided. Finance also insists that results keep four decimal places; that setting is already on the function.
mission.objective: Make fx-rate-lookup return production EUR/USD conversions again with the four decimal places finance expects. It must read the production rates table.

mission.name: Three Seconds and Out
mission.description: Quillmark Reports renders customer statements in the Lambda function statement-renderer. Short statements work, but every long one (the quarterly statements run to a dozen pages) just stops: the customer portal shows a spinner and then an error. The function logic is fine; ops noticed that its configuration still carries the default limits from the project template.
mission.objective: Let a 12-page statement render successfully. The portal calls the function through an HTTP API that gives up after 29 seconds, so the function's timeout must not exceed that.

mission.name: Out of Memory
mission.description: Skyline Maps stitches map tiles into one big image inside the Lambda function tile-stitcher. Small previews work, but the full-size export used by the print shop just dies: no error message, no stack trace, only a runtime exit. The function was created with the template's default memory. The finance team has capped the function at 1 GB because memory is billed per GB-second.
mission.objective: Make a 16 x 16 tile export (a 256 MB canvas) succeed, with the function's memory setting at no more than 1024 MB.

mission.name: The Throttled Function
mission.description: Brightside Coupons went through a nasty incident on Sunday night: a runaway retry loop opened hundreds of database connections, and the on-call engineer "paused" the coupon-redeemer Lambda function with a quick CLI command. The incident is long closed but checkout still shows "coupons are unavailable". Callers get "Rate Exceeded" even though traffic is tiny. The database pool has room for 20 concurrent redemptions, and the post-mortem insists that nothing should be able to exceed that again.
mission.objective: Let coupon-redeemer process requests again while keeping a concurrency cap in place that is never above 20 simultaneous executions.

mission.name: Lost on Failure
mission.description: Relaycast's order service sends text messages by invoking the Lambda function sms-notifier asynchronously and never looks at the result. Customer support keeps hearing "I never got my delivery text", and nobody can say how many messages are failing, because failed events simply disappear. The team has already created the SQS queue sms-failed-deliveries for investigation, and the function's role is allowed to write to it. Sending a text twice is worse than not sending it, so retries are switched off on purpose.
mission.objective: Make every asynchronous invocation of sms-notifier that fails land in the queue sms-failed-deliveries together with the error details, while keeping retries disabled and leaving successful invocations out of the queue.

mission.name: Missing Dependency
mission.description: Ironbridge Pay scores card transactions in the Lambda function txn-scorer. Its business rules and its tracing helper both come from Lambda layers. After the fraud team announced the 2024 ruleset, the function started to crash while it is still initialising, before it even looks at the transaction. The fraud team swears that the new ruleset has been published as a layer, and the function's code did not change.
mission.objective: Make txn-scorer use the 2024 version of the riskkit-core layer while keeping the tracekit-logging layer it also depends on.

mission.name: The Silent Upload
mission.description: Helixia Labs' sequencers drop result files into the S3 bucket helixia-lab-inbox all day. A Lambda function, lab-result-indexer, is supposed to add each new result to the search table lab-result-index, but clinicians report that nothing new shows up. The function itself works (it was tested by hand) and S3 is already allowed to call it. The bucket also receives huge raw scan images under scans/, and indexing those would cost a fortune.
mission.objective: Make every new .json file uploaded under results/ in helixia-lab-inbox get indexed automatically, and nothing else in the bucket.

mission.name: Watching the Wrong Door
mission.description: Marlowe Freight registers every invoice PDF in a billing ledger through the Lambda function invoice-extractor. Since the staging environment was cloned last month, the finance team sees a strange picture: test invoices from marlowe-invoices-staging show up in the real ledger, while the real invoices uploaded to marlowe-invoices-prod are never registered at all. Someone wired the trigger to the wrong bucket during the clone.
mission.objective: Have PDF invoices uploaded to marlowe-invoices-prod registered in the ledger, while nothing uploaded to marlowe-invoices-staging reaches the ledger any more. Only .pdf files may trigger the function.

mission.name: Permission Denied by Lambda
mission.description: Cartwheel Logistics lets a few carrier partners call its rate quote function, rate-quote-engine, directly with their own IAM identities. The new partner ShipRight signed last week and their integration user partner-shipright gets AccessDeniedException on every call. IAM looks fine on their side: nobody wants to hand a partner permissions inside Cartwheel's own IAM, so the contract says access is granted on the function itself. FastLane, a former partner whose contract ended, must keep being locked out.
mission.objective: Allow the IAM user partner-shipright, and only that user, to invoke rate-quote-engine. Grant nothing beyond invoking the function.

mission.name: The Ghost Alias
mission.description: Fernhill Billing's checkout calls the tax-calculator function through its prod alias, so releases can be promoted without touching the callers. This morning checkout started failing with "Function version not found" and nobody is sure what the alias is supposed to point at. Three versions have been published over the past year; the release notes live in their descriptions. The staging alias must keep pointing at the version being trialled there.
mission.objective: Make the prod alias of tax-calculator serve the version that finance approved for production, without touching the staging alias and without pointing prod at $LATEST.

mission.name: Stranded in VPC
mission.description: Orbit Retail's order-sync function must write into the orders database, which lives in a private subnet of the VPC named orders-vpc. After last week's network refactoring the function is "in a VPC" on paper: it carries the right security group, but connection attempts to the database time out. Inspecting the function's network settings shows no subnets at all. Security has two rules: the function must survive the loss of one availability zone, and it must never sit in a public subnet (no route to an internet gateway).
mission.objective: Place order-sync into orders-vpc using its existing security group and private subnets spread over at least two availability zones. Do not use any public subnet and do not leave orders-vpc.

mission.name: Unguarded VPC
mission.description: Granite Analytics' nightly exporter runs in the analytics VPC and needs to reach the warehouse database on port 5432. Its subnets are fine, but the function was deployed without any security group, and the data team's export hangs on the database connection. The warehouse database's firewall (warehouse-db-sg) is locked down on purpose and the security team has stated that its rules must stay as strict as they are: no CIDR ranges, only security groups that are explicitly trusted. The analytics VPC also contains a bastion-admin-sg that must never be attached to application code.
mission.objective: Give the exporter function a security group in analytics-vpc that the warehouse database already trusts on port 5432 (or that you make it trust without opening the database to any IP range), keep its subnets, and do not attach the bastion group.

mission.name: The Locked Door
mission.description: Pebble Studio collects beta sign-ups on a public page whose JavaScript posts the visitor's email straight to the HTTPS URL of the Lambda function invite-landing. Launch day is here and visitors only see an error. The URL was created by a template that defaults to the safest authentication setting, and that same template already restricts browsers (CORS) to the sign-up page at https://pebblestudio.example. The team also runs invite-admin, an internal function with its own URL, which must stay private.
mission.objective: Make the invite-landing function URL accept unauthenticated requests from the public while keeping its CORS restriction to the sign-up origin, and keep the invite-admin URL IAM-protected.

mission.name: Bad Apple in the Batch
mission.description: Kestrel Ticketing processes ticket events from an SQS queue with the Lambda function ticket-processor. Twice a week one malformed event slips into the queue, and each time the on-call engineer finds the same mess in the ledger: perfectly good tickets in the same batch were processed three times, and then all of them, good ones included, ended up in the dead-letter queue. The queue is already wired to a dead-letter queue after 3 receives. The source of the malformed events is being tracked down separately.
mission.objective: Make one bad event in a batch affect only itself: the good events of the same batch must be processed exactly once and be gone from the queues, while the malformed event must still end up in ticket-events-dlq (not silently dropped).

mission.name: Fenced In
mission.description: Quasar Fintech's audit job (the Lambda function key-audit) reads an API key from Parameter Store and stores its fingerprint in an audit bucket. In code review the role's own policy was checked and approved: it allows exactly those two things. Yet in production the function dies with AccessDenied on the Parameter Store read. The platform team mentions that every role created by the self-service portal is automatically fenced with a permissions boundary called quasar-self-service-boundary. The same role policy also carries a leftover dynamodb:* grant, and the security team insists it stays ineffective.
mission.objective: Let key-audit read /quasar/api-key and write its audit record, while the boundary stays attached to the role and the role still cannot use DynamoDB.

mission.name: No Table, No Orders
mission.description: Harvest Hub connects farm co-ops to restaurants. This morning the order-ingest service was redeployed into a fresh account and every order is bouncing with ResourceNotFoundException. The ops engineer says the table was "created by Terraform", but nobody can find it. The service writes one item per order and reads a farm's orders back in time order, so the key design matters: orders are grouped by the farm that placed them (string attribute farmId) and ordered by the moment they were placed (number attribute orderedAt, epoch seconds).
mission.objective: Create the DynamoDB table harvest-orders so that the ingest service can write orders and read one farm's orders back in chronological order, newest-first or oldest-first. Use on-demand billing; the order volume is unpredictable.

mission.name: Numbers Don't Look Like UUIDs
mission.description: Postbox sends push notifications for a ride-sharing app. The new preferences service stores each rider's notification settings in the table postbox-prefs, keyed by recipientId. The first real rider signed up this morning and the service threw a ValidationException on every write. The recipientId values come from the identity provider and look like 7f3c2a9e-1b64-4d0a-9c1e-5a2b8d4e6f10. Someone created the table by hand last week, and also switched on deletion protection "so nobody drops it by accident". The table is still empty.
mission.objective: Make postbox-prefs accept preference items for riders identified by their UUID string recipientId, and let the service read an item back by that id. The table must keep its name.

mission.name: History Keeps Vanishing
mission.description: Fixline's support desk shows a timeline for every ticket: opened, assigned, escalated, resolved. Agents complain that timelines always show a single entry, the most recent one. Engineers confirmed the service writes every event to the table fixline-ticket-events with a ticketId (string) and an eventAt attribute (ISO-8601 string such as 2026-03-02T09:15:00Z), and that no write ever fails. The table was built from a quick-start snippet that only declared ticketId as key. The service reads a ticket's events with a time window, for example "everything since 08:00".
mission.objective: Fix fixline-ticket-events so that several events for the same ticket are all stored, and so that the events of one ticket can be read back in time order and filtered by a time window. The table may be recreated; the history it currently holds is only the last event per ticket and can be discarded.

mission.name: Login by Email
mission.description: Cartwheel is a bike-share membership service. Riders log in with their email address, and the login endpoint looks the member up through a global secondary index called email-index on the table cartwheel-members. After the weekend migration the endpoint returns a 500 for everybody: the table moved over with its four members, but the index did not. Members are identified by memberId; the login code reads the email, memberId and plan of the member it finds.
mission.objective: Make it possible to look a Cartwheel member up by email address through an index named email-index, including for members who sign up after the fix. All existing members must stay in the table, so it must not be dropped and rebuilt.

mission.name: The Index That Knew the Wrong Thing
mission.description: Stockroom runs warehouse pick lists. Pickers scan a product SKU and the app asks the table stockroom-bins, through the index sku-index, which bins hold that SKU and in what quantity, biggest stock first when they ask for "at least N units". Since a refactor the picker app errors out with a ValidationException on every scan. Whoever rebuilt the index copied the example from another project and keyed it on a different attribute (the item attribute aisle). The table itself, keyed by binId, is fine and holds live stock records that must not be touched.
mission.objective: Make sku-index answer "bins holding SKU X with at least N units": partition key sku, sort key qty (number). Keep the index name, keep all stock records.

mission.name: Five Units Against a Flood
mission.description: Pulsewire collects sensor readings from wind turbines. Between 02:00 and 03:00 every night thousands of turbines flush their buffers at once, and the table pulsewire-readings (provisioned mode, 5 read and 5 write capacity units) starts rejecting writes with ProvisionedThroughputExceededException. During the day traffic is calm, so flat high capacity would waste money. Finance has also made clear that the table stays in provisioned mode: the company bought reserved capacity, and on-demand pricing is off the table for this workload.
mission.objective: Keep pulsewire-readings in provisioned mode and make its read and write capacity follow demand automatically with Application Auto Scaling: both dimensions need a scalable target that can grow to at least 500 units without dropping below 20, and a target-tracking policy aiming for a sensible utilisation (between 30 and 80 percent).

mission.name: Flash Sale Pricing
mission.description: Ticketflash sells concert tickets. Seat holds live in the table ticketflash-holds (provisioned, 10 units each way, plus a global secondary index event-index on eventId). On sale days traffic jumps from a few requests per second to thousands within a minute, then drops to nothing for weeks. The team once tried to chase this with auto scaling, but it always reacts too late and the cost report shows paying for idle capacity all month. The platform lead's decision: stop forecasting and pay per request. The 6 current holds and the index must survive the change.
mission.objective: Move ticketflash-holds to on-demand billing without rebuilding the table or losing the event-index lookup, and clean up the auto scaling configuration that was left behind for it.

mission.name: Sessions That Never Die
mission.description: Loginly keeps web sessions in the table loginly-sessions. Each session item carries an attribute expiresAt holding the expiry time as epoch seconds, and the privacy policy says expired sessions must disappear on their own, not stay around for months. Months later the table has grown to a size nobody expected and an auditor found sessions from last year. The platform team swears they "turned on TTL" when they created the table.
mission.objective: Make DynamoDB automatically delete sessions whose expiresAt time has passed. Prove it works: a session whose expiresAt lies in the past must really vanish from the table without anyone deleting it. Sessions that have not yet expired must stay.

mission.name: The Silent Table
mission.description: Greenroom is a newsroom CMS. Legal wants an audit trail: whenever an article in the table greenroom-articles is edited, the audit consumer must see what the headline was before and what it is now, so it can store the diff. The consumer reads the table's change stream, but since go-live the audit log has stayed empty and the consumer logs "no stream found for greenroom-articles". The table was created from an older template that never switched streams on.
mission.objective: Turn on DynamoDB Streams for greenroom-articles so that edits to an article produce change records with both the item as it was before and as it is after the edit. Existing articles must stay in place.

mission.name: The Index You Can't Add Later
mission.description: Clinicall books appointments in the table clinic-appointments (partition key patientId, sort key apptDate, an ISO date string). Nurses want a patient's appointments sorted by urgency, so a developer shipped code that queries an index named severity-index (same patientId partition, sorted by the numeric attribute severity) and asked ops to "just add the index". The ops engineer tried a few update-table variations and could not get DynamoDB to create it. The table holds four live appointments that cannot be lost, and the booking app reads the reason attribute from the index results.
mission.objective: Provide severity-index on clinic-appointments (same partition key patientId, sorted by severity), returning reason with each result. All four appointments must be preserved with all their attributes, under the same table name.

mission.name: Half the Picture
mission.description: Shelfwise is an online bookshop. Its category pages query the global secondary index category-index of the table shelfwise-books (partition key category, sort key price) and render a card with the book's title and author plus its price. Since the index was rebuilt, the cards show only ISBNs and prices: the title and author are missing. The front-end team's first suggestion was to copy every attribute into the index, but each book also carries a multi-kilobyte blurb that category pages never show, and the finance team has already complained about the write bill.
mission.objective: Fix category-index so a category query returns isbn, price, title and author for every book, but not the large blurb attribute. All books must stay in the table.

mission.name: The Audit Nobody Wanted
mission.description: Ledgerly is a small fintech that has just been told by its auditor: every DynamoDB table that holds SOX-relevant financial records must be recoverable to any second within the last 35 days. A new engineer enabled backups on a table called ledger-entries and called it done. The auditor's checklist, however, is driven by the resource tag compliance=sox, not by table names, and there are other tables carrying it. A scratch table used for experiments (tag compliance=none) is expensive to protect and intentionally stays unprotected.
mission.objective: Make every table tagged compliance=sox point-in-time recoverable: a restore of the table to its latest restorable time must succeed. Leave the scratch table without point-in-time recovery.

mission.name: The Overprotective Guard
mission.description: Parcelo's warehouse robots mark orders as shipped by running the script workspace/ship-orders.sh against the table parcelo-orders. It loops over the two orders the dock reported as loaded, ord-1042 and ord-1043, and for each one flips the status to SHIPPED, assigns a tracking number and bumps the version counter. Nothing ships: every call fails with ConditionalCheckFailedException. The condition was added "to stop double shipping" by someone who was thinking about creating new orders. Careful: the dock list is known to be sloppy. ord-1043 was in fact shipped yesterday, and shipping it twice would hand the customer a second tracking number.
mission.objective: Get ord-1042 shipped (status SHIPPED, version incremented by exactly one, a tracking number set, everything else on the order intact) while the guard keeps protecting orders that are not in PACKED state: ord-1043 must come out of the run unchanged. Edit and run the script; do not just remove the guard.

mission.name: Words You Cannot Say
mission.description: Deskly is a help-desk tool. Closing a ticket is done by the helper script workspace/close-ticket.sh, which updates the ticket in the table deskly-tickets. Since the team added a closing comment and a closed-at stamp, the script fails for every ticket with a ValidationException saying an attribute name is a reserved keyword. Support is stuck with ticket tk-77 (a refund request) that the agent resolved an hour ago and cannot close. The attributes are called status, comment and timestamp, and renaming them in the stored data is not an option because other services read them.
mission.objective: Make close-ticket.sh work and close tk-77: its status must become CLOSED, its comment must hold the closing note, and a numeric timestamp must be recorded, with all other attributes of the ticket left as they were. The attribute names in the table must not change.

mission.name: Scan Is Not a Query
mission.description: Orbit Freight's nightly report job lists every shipment of one region that left the dock after a given time. It runs as the IAM user orbit-report-svc and today it calls Scan on the table orbit-shipments with a filter on region and shippedAt, which reads every item (millions in production) and burns half the table's read budget. The security review has decided that this job may never scan again: it should get exactly one read capability, Query, used against a dedicated index named by-region-time (partition key region, sort key shippedAt as a number), and nothing else. The job's current script is in workspace/report.sh. The same account holds a table orbit-payroll that the job must never touch.
mission.objective: Redesign the access so that orbit-report-svc can query shipments of one region newer than a timestamp through by-region-time, and cannot scan the table, cannot fetch single items, cannot write anything and cannot touch orbit-payroll. Existing shipments must stay in the table.

mission.name: Tenants Behind Glass
mission.description: Crmly is a multi-tenant CRM. All tenants share one table, crmly-contacts (partition key tenantId, sort key contactId), and every tenant's web portal talks to DynamoDB with its own IAM identity. A penetration tester just reported that the portal identity for the tenant acme, the IAM user portal-acme, can read and write the contacts of every other tenant, for example globex, simply by changing the tenantId in a request. The portal needs to keep reading and writing acme's own contacts and nothing more.
mission.objective: Restrict portal-acme so that it can query, read, write and delete contacts of tenantId acme, but nothing belonging to other tenants and no table-wide scans. The policy must not simply be replaced by an Allow on a different resource; the table is shared and the isolation has to come from the policy itself.

mission.name: Typo at the Dock
mission.description: Harborline Freight's order-intake service has been throwing AWS.SimpleQueueService.NonExistentQueue since last night's infrastructure re-deploy. The deploy script created a queue called harborline-order (singular) from a typo in the config, and nobody noticed because the service names its queue harborline-orders. Customers can place orders, but nothing reaches the warehouse worker.
mission.objective: Make the queue harborline-orders exist so the intake service can send orders and the warehouse worker can receive them. Because the warehouse worker polls all day, the queue should use long polling with a 10 second wait.

mission.name: Staging Is Not Production
mission.description: TicketDesk's support-ticket API reads the address of its queue from the Parameter Store entry /ticketdesk/prod/support-queue-url. Since Tuesday's promotion from staging, customers' tickets are accepted by the API but the support agents' worker, which consumes the production queue ticketdesk-support, never sees them. The API does not report errors: the sends are succeeding, just somewhere else.
mission.objective: Make the production API deliver tickets to the production queue ticketdesk-support. The API gets the queue address only from the parameter /ticketdesk/prod/support-queue-url, so fix the configuration rather than the queues. Staging must stop receiving production tickets.

mission.name: The Label That Printed Twice
mission.description: ParcelPilot's label renderer pulls jobs from the queue labelforge-jobs. Rendering one shipping label takes up to 8 seconds, but customers keep complaining that parcels arrive with two or even three identical labels. The renderer logs show the same job ID being handed out again while the first worker is still busy with it, and no worker has crashed.
mission.objective: Stop jobs from being handed to a second worker while the first one is still rendering (up to 8 seconds). A worker that crashes must not hold a job hostage for long either: a job must be retried within 2 minutes.

mission.name: Poison Pill
mission.description: LedgerLink settles card payments from the queue ledgerlink-settlements. Last night one malformed settlement file crashed the worker over and over: the message kept returning, the worker kept dying, and the whole shift's backlog stood behind it. Engineering wants such messages parked somewhere safe for inspection after a few failed attempts. At the moment the queue has no parking place at all.
mission.objective: Give ledgerlink-settlements a dead-letter queue. A message that has been received and not deleted several times (at least 2, at most 10 attempts) must be moved to it, and the dead-letter queue must keep parked messages for 14 days, longer than the source queue does.

mission.name: The Dead Letter Gets Lost
mission.description: Foxglove Mailroom sends customer e-mails from the queue mailroom-outbound. Support noticed that bounced-address jobs vanish: they are retried three times, then disappear, and the dead-letter queue mailroom-outbound-dlq is not growing. A redrive policy is configured on the queue and nobody sees an error, which is exactly why nobody looked at it.
mission.objective: Make failed jobs from mailroom-outbound actually arrive in mailroom-outbound-dlq after their retries. Keep the existing DLQ and the jobs already parked in it.

mission.name: One Strike
mission.description: Pinecrest Clinics sends appointment reminders by SMS from the queue pinecrest-sms. The SMS provider has short hiccups, and a reminder that fails once is normally fine on the second try. Since the queue was given a dead-letter queue, though, the ops team sees dozens of perfectly good reminders in pinecrest-sms-dlq after every hiccup, and patients miss their appointments.
mission.objective: Make pinecrest-sms tolerate at least two failed attempts of a message before it is parked in pinecrest-sms-dlq, while a message that never succeeds must still be parked after at most 10 attempts.

mission.name: Out of Order
mission.description: Ironwood Bank posts account events (deposit, withdrawal, fee) to the queue ironwood-ledger-events. Account balances keep coming out wrong: a withdrawal is sometimes processed before the deposit that funded it, and customers get overdraft fees. The ledger consumer handles messages one at a time, so the fault is not in the consumer. Engineering already knows that events for the same account must be processed in the order they were sent, while different accounts may be processed independently.
mission.objective: Provide a queue named ironwood-ledger-events.fifo that preserves the order of events within a message group, so the producer can use one group per account. The existing standard queue may stay in place until the producer is switched over.

mission.name: Twice Charged
mission.description: Tidewater Pay moved its payment-capture jobs to the FIFO queue tidewater-payments.fifo. The webhook receiver cannot be changed this week: it forwards each gateway callback unchanged and does not generate any MessageDeduplicationId. Since the cut-over, every callback fails with InvalidParameterValue, and during the first hour of the cut-over some customers were charged twice when the gateway re-delivered a callback.
mission.objective: Make the existing queue tidewater-payments.fifo accept sends that carry no MessageDeduplicationId, and make it drop a repeated identical callback instead of enqueuing it twice. Do not recreate the queue: the job that is already waiting in it must survive.

mission.name: Locked Mailbox
mission.description: Ember Retail's monitoring pipeline publishes alerts to the SNS topic ember-alerts, and the on-call pager service reads them from the queue ember-pager-intake, which is already subscribed to the topic. The security review last week removed the queue's open access policy, and the new, tighter policy was never written. In a real account, SNS would now get AccessDenied when delivering to the queue and every alert would disappear silently. The draft in policy.json is what the team started with before the meeting ended.
mission.objective: Give ember-pager-intake a queue policy that lets the SNS service deliver messages to this queue, but only on behalf of the topic ember-alerts. No other topic, account or principal may be allowed to send to it.

mission.name: Storm Warning, No Station
mission.description: Lighthouse Weather's forecasting engine publishes severe-weather bulletins to the SNS topic lighthouse-storm-warnings. Since the stack was rolled back after a failed deploy, every publish fails with NotFound: the topic was deleted together with everything attached to it. The harbour-radio gateway still reads from its queue harbor-radio-feed, but the queue no longer receives anything.
mission.objective: Bring the bulletin path back: the topic lighthouse-storm-warnings must exist and a bulletin published to it must reach the queue harbor-radio-feed.

mission.name: Nobody Told Loyalty
mission.description: Bluebird Market publishes every completed checkout to the SNS topic bluebird-checkout-events. The fulfilment team's queue bluebird-fulfilment receives them fine. The loyalty team launched their new points service this week and reads from the queue bluebird-loyalty, but customers are not getting any points: that queue has stayed empty since launch day.
mission.objective: Make every event published to bluebird-checkout-events reach both bluebird-fulfilment and bluebird-loyalty, without disturbing the fulfilment team's existing subscription.

mission.name: Wrong Mailbox
mission.description: Quartz Studio's billing system publishes invoice events to the SNS topic quartz-invoice-events. The invoice-printing service reads the queue quartz-invoices-prod, which stays empty, while the queue quartz-invoices-staging, used by the test environment, is suddenly full of production invoices. A subscription exists and SNS reports no errors.
mission.objective: Deliver invoice events from quartz-invoice-events to quartz-invoices-prod, and only there. The staging queue must stop receiving production events.

mission.name: The Silent Refund Worker
mission.description: Cobalt Outfitters publishes every order lifecycle event to the SNS topic cobalt-order-events as a JSON document, for example {"eventType":"order_cancelled","orderId":"..."}. The refund service reads the queue cobalt-refund-worker, whose subscription has a filter policy so that only cancellations and refunds arrive. Since the subscription was created the queue has been completely empty, even though customers cancel orders all day. The publisher is a vendor product and cannot be changed.
mission.objective: Make cancellations and refunds (eventType order_cancelled and order_refunded) reach cobalt-refund-worker while every other event type, such as order_created, stays out. Keep filtering on eventType: removing the filter is not acceptable.

mission.name: Gift Wrap
mission.description: Delta Cart publishes cart events to the SNS topic delta-cart-events. The web analytics collector reads them from the queue delta-web-analytics, whose subscription already filters on channel = web. The collector's parser expects the body of every queue message to be the cart event itself, e.g. {"sku":"A-100","qty":2}, but it crashes on every message: the body it gets is a bigger JSON document that starts with "Type":"Notification" and has the cart event buried inside as an escaped string.
mission.objective: Make the collector receive the bare cart event as the message body, without the SNS envelope. The queue must still receive only events published with the attribute channel = web.

mission.name: Forty Tonnes of Paperwork
mission.description: Quill Logistics' nightly job builds the shipping manifest for the next day (a JSON document of about 1.3 MB, regenerated into payload/manifest.json in your workspace) and sends it to the queue quill-manifest-jobs for the customs-filing worker. Since the manifest grew past its old size the send fails with a message-size error. The bucket quill-manifest-offload exists for exactly this kind of payload, but nobody wired it up.
mission.objective: Get the full, unmodified payload/manifest.json to the customs-filing worker through quill-manifest-jobs. SQS cannot carry a message this large, so the document must be stored in S3 (bucket quill-manifest-offload) and the queue must carry a small message that tells the worker where to find it. The queue message must stay under 1 KiB.

mission.name: Mail Without a Stamp
mission.description: Gatehouse Security's visitor-registration API runs as the IAM user gatehouse-api and must drop each registration into the queue gatehouse-intake. Since the access review, every registration fails with AccessDenied, while the compliance team insists that the policy "was written for exactly this". The user's inline policy lives in policy.json. The same account also has a queue gatehouse-audit that the API must never write to.
mission.objective: Let gatehouse-api send messages to the queue gatehouse-intake, and nothing more: it must not be able to read or purge that queue, and it must not be able to write to gatehouse-audit.

mission.name: Second Chance for Six Invoices
mission.description: Crescent Billing's invoice worker had a bug last Friday, and six invoices ended up in the dead-letter queue crescent-invoices-dlq after their retries ran out. The bug is fixed and deployed. Finance now wants those six invoices processed, which means they have to go back to the main queue crescent-invoices. A junior engineer proposes writing a script that receives, sends and deletes them one by one.
mission.objective: Return the six parked invoices to crescent-invoices, each exactly once and unchanged, so that crescent-invoices-dlq is empty afterwards. Use the queue's built-in redrive capability rather than losing or duplicating messages.

mission.name: Logs Into the Void
mission.description: SwiftPost runs its parcel-locker checkout API in containers whose log driver is told to write to the CloudWatch log group /swiftpost/checkout-api. After last week's account clean-up the containers still start, but the on-call engineer sees no logs at all, and the log driver prints ResourceNotFoundException on every flush. The driver is configured to create its own log streams but, as a safety rule, not log groups.
mission.objective: Make the checkout API able to write its logs: the log group /swiftpost/checkout-api must exist so that a container can create a stream in it and its log lines can be read back.

mission.name: The Logs That Never Die
mission.description: Orbit Analytics' cloud bill shows CloudWatch Logs storage growing by 40% every month. Finance found why: the log groups /orbit/ingest, /orbit/api and /orbit/worker were created by the app itself, so their retention is "Never expire". The company's data policy says application logs are kept for 30 days. The audit trail in /orbit/audit is different: legal requires one year there, and it is configured correctly. Other teams' log groups in the same account are not Orbit's business.
mission.objective: Make /orbit/ingest, /orbit/api and /orbit/worker keep their logs for exactly 30 days. Leave /orbit/audit (1 year) and every log group that does not belong to Orbit exactly as it is.

mission.name: Gateway Seven Is Mute
mission.description: Harvest Co. monitors greenhouse sensors through field gateways that each log to their own stream in the log group /harvest/sensors. Gateways 01 to 06 have been shipping logs for months. This morning gateway 07 was installed at a new site; it boots, reads its sensors, and its agent logs ResourceNotFoundException (stream does not exist). The agent on a gateway is allowed to write events but not to create streams, and the group is fine.
mission.objective: Make gateway 07 able to ship its logs: the stream field-gateway-07 must exist in /harvest/sensors and accept log events. Do not disturb the six existing streams.

mission.name: Counting the Wrong Word
mission.description: Ledgerbox's payment service writes lines such as "2026-11-11T10:02:11Z ERROR gateway timeout order=88123" to the log group /ledgerbox/payments. A metric filter named payment-failures is supposed to turn each of those lines into a count for the metric Ledgerbox/PaymentFailures, which the finance dashboard charts. The chart has been flat zero for a week although customers are complaining about failed payments, and the logs clearly contain failures.
mission.objective: Make the filter payment-failures count every log line that reports an ERROR (and only those) into Ledgerbox/PaymentFailures, with one count per matching line. Keep the metric name and namespace: dashboards depend on them.

mission.name: Nobody Is Watching Checkout
mission.description: Meridian's checkout service publishes its 99th-percentile latency to the custom metric Meridian/Checkout P99LatencyMs. During last night's incident the metric climbed past 2 seconds for an hour and nobody was paged, because no alarm exists for it. The on-call rotation is notified through the SNS topic meridian-oncall. The file alarm.json in your workspace is a half-filled template from the post-mortem.
mission.objective: Create an alarm on Meridian/Checkout P99LatencyMs that goes to ALARM when the latency is above 800 ms and publishes to the topic meridian-oncall when it does. It must stay OK for normal values. For this lab the alarm should evaluate a single 10-second period using the Maximum statistic.

mission.name: A Zero Too Many
mission.description: Pylon Compute's capacity team wants a heads-up when a node is CPU saturated, which they define as NodeCpuPercent above 90. Their alarm pylon-node-cpu-saturated has never fired, even though last Thursday three nodes sat at 97% for twenty minutes and a customer called. The alarm is defined in alarm.json in your workspace and was applied from there.
mission.objective: Make pylon-node-cpu-saturated go to ALARM when NodeCpuPercent is above 90, and stay out of ALARM at normal load (45%). Keep the metric, statistic and period as they are.

mission.name: The Pager That Never Rang
mission.description: Halcyon's primary database ran out of connections on Saturday night. The alarm halcyon-db-connections-high did turn red in the console, exactly as designed, but nobody was woken up. The on-call engineers receive pages through the SNS topic halcyon-oncall (their pager app reads the queue behind it). During a maintenance window last month somebody switched the alarm's notifications off, and while they were at it they also pointed the action at an old topic, halcyon-oncall-legacy, that nobody listens to any more. The alarm definition is in alarm.json.
mission.objective: Make halcyon-db-connections-high notify the on-call topic halcyon-oncall whenever it goes to ALARM. Do not change what it measures or when it fires (OpenConnections above 150).

mission.name: Crying Wolf at Full Health
mission.description: Nimbus Storage's data volume data-01 reports its free space in gigabytes to Nimbus/Storage FreeSpaceGB. The alarm nimbus-data-volume-low-space is meant to warn when fewer than 10 GB are left. Since it was created the on-call team has been woken up while the volume is nearly empty of data (hundreds of gigabytes free), and, worse, the alarm stayed green when the volume filled up last week. Everyone has started ignoring it. The definition is in alarm.json.
mission.objective: Make nimbus-data-volume-low-space go to ALARM when free space is below 10 GB and stay OK when plenty of space is free. Keep the metric, dimension and threshold of 10.

mission.name: Five Minutes Too Late
mission.description: Brightside Mail's deliverability team wants to know quickly when bounces spike, because mailbox providers start throttling a sender after a few minutes of bad traffic. Their alarm brightside-bounce-spike fires on 50 or more bounced messages, which is correct, but on Tuesday a burst of 300 bounces was only reported after the damage was done. They suspect the alarm is slow. The definition is in alarm.json.
mission.objective: Make brightside-bounce-spike react to a burst of bounces within seconds (it must be able to change state after at most one minute of data), without changing the metric, the statistic or the threshold of 50.

mission.name: The Empty Error Table
mission.description: Rivergate's payments team keeps a CloudWatch dashboard, rivergate-payments, with one Logs Insights widget titled "Recent payment errors". The service logs JSON lines such as {"level":"ERROR","code":"CARD_DECLINED","order":"..."} to the log group /rivergate/payments. During an incident review today the table was empty although the logs plainly contain errors, and the team lost ten minutes believing everything was fine. The dashboard definition is in dashboard.json in your workspace.
mission.objective: Make the widget on the dashboard rivergate-payments show the error entries of /rivergate/payments (and only those): running the widget's query must return exactly the ERROR log lines.

mission.name: Receipts on Strike
mission.description: Skyline Cinemas' box office publishes a TicketSold event to the default event bus for every ticket. An EventBridge rule, skyline-ticket-sold, is supposed to forward them to the queue skyline-receipts, which the receipt printers in the lobbies read. Since Monday's release no receipts are printing. The queue is healthy, the box office is publishing events, and the rule exists with the right pattern and the right target, but a deployment script left it in the state shown in rule.json.
mission.objective: Make TicketSold events from skyline.box-office reach skyline-receipts again, and keep the rule selective: other event types must still not be forwarded.

mission.name: Shipment Sent to the Sandbox
mission.description: Harbor Freight publishes a ShipmentCreated event whenever a container is booked. The rule harbor-shipment-created forwards it to the ingestion queue that the customs-pre-filing service reads: harbor-ingest-prod. Customs is complaining that no bookings arrive, while the staging team is surprised by a stream of real bookings in harbor-ingest-staging. The rule is enabled and its pattern is correct. The target as deployed is in target.json.
mission.objective: Deliver ShipmentCreated events from harbor-shipment-created to harbor-ingest-prod and nowhere else; staging must stop receiving them.

mission.name: The Pattern That Matched Nothing
mission.description: QuillShop's "gold customer" workflow is supposed to start for every order placed by a gold-tier customer: the shop publishes events such as {"source":"quillshop.orders","detail-type":"OrderPlaced","detail":{"tier":"gold",...}} to the default bus, and the rule quillshop-gold-orders copies matching ones into the queue gold-concierge. The concierge team has not received a single order since launch. The rule is enabled and its target is right. Its event pattern is in pattern.json.
mission.objective: Make the rule quillshop-gold-orders forward OrderPlaced events of gold-tier customers from quillshop.orders to gold-concierge. Orders from other tiers must not be forwarded.

mission.name: Paging When Everything Is Fine
mission.description: Strata Cloud's on-call engineers get a single page per incident from the composite alarm strata-api-unhealthy, which combines two simple alarms: strata-api-errors (too many 5xx responses) and strata-api-latency (responses too slow). Since the composite was introduced the engineers are paged the moment all is well and, according to the post-mortem, were not paged during Saturday's slowdown. The composite's rule text is in alarm-rule.txt.
mission.objective: Make strata-api-unhealthy go to ALARM when at least one of the two child alarms is in ALARM, and stay OK while both are healthy. Both child alarms must remain part of the rule, and the composite must keep notifying the topic strata-oncall.

mission.name: The Shipper Without a Ticket
mission.description: Lumen Retail's store-gateway agent ships its logs to the group /lumen/store-gateway using the IAM user lumen-shipper. A new store was onboarded this week: the agent starts, creates its stream, and then every upload fails with AccessDeniedException; the logs of that store are missing. The user's inline policy lumen-shipper-logs was written in a hurry and is stored in policy.json.
mission.objective: Let lumen-shipper create log streams and upload log events in /lumen/store-gateway, and nothing more: it must not be able to delete the log group or change its retention. (Sandbox note: this emulator evaluates CloudWatch Logs permissions against Resource "*", so keep the resource as it is; in a real account you would scope it to the group's ARN.)

mission.name: The Grey Light
mission.description: Vesper's backup jobs publish a datapoint to Vesper/Backup BackupFailures only when a job fails; successful nights publish nothing. The alarm vesper-backup-failed (any failure at all) is meant to be green on good nights. Instead it has shown the grey INSUFFICIENT_DATA state for three weeks, the status board treats grey as "unknown", and nobody can tell a healthy backup from a broken alarm. The definition is in alarm.json.
mission.objective: Make vesper-backup-failed report OK when there are no failures, and still go to ALARM when a failure is published. Keep the metric, statistic and threshold.

mission.name: Last Night's Outage Was Silent
