mission.description: Talon Orders' API logs every failure as a line containing the word ERROR in the group /talon/orders-api. The monitoring chain was meant to be: a metric filter (order-errors) turns each failing line into a count, an alarm (talon-order-errors-high) fires at 3 or more errors in 10 seconds, and the alarm publishes to the SNS topic talon-oncall, which the pager reads. During last night's outage hundreds of errors were logged and nobody was paged. Each link of the chain was configured by a different person; both files are in your workspace (filter.json and alarm.json). The topic and the pager already work.
mission.objective: Repair the chain end to end: when the API logs a burst of ERROR lines, the alarm talon-order-errors-high must go to ALARM and the page must reach the pager queue behind talon-oncall. Ordinary INFO lines must not count.

mission.name: Launch Day Lockout
mission.description: Tindle Books opens its spring sale at noon and the storefront needs one more web server. The runbook command in launch-web.sh worked last quarter, but today it dies immediately and nothing is launched. Last week's infrastructure cleanup removed a lot of "unused" resources from the tindle-prod VPC, and nobody remembers what the old launch command depended on.
mission.objective: Get an instance named tindle-web-1 running in the tindle-prod VPC's public subnet, protected by a security group that serves HTTPS (443) to the internet and does not expose SSH to the world.

mission.name: Quillpad Is Unreachable
mission.description: Quillpad, a small blogging platform, moved its web node into a freshly built security group called quillpad-web-sg. The instance is healthy and nginx is up, but every reader gets a timeout. The on-call engineer confirms nothing is wrong on the host itself.
mission.objective: Let readers reach the quillpad-web instance over both plain HTTP and HTTPS from anywhere, keeping the group attached to the instance. Nothing else should be open to the internet.

mission.name: Eight-Thousand-Eighty Is Not Home
mission.description: Ledgerly's internal ledger-api sits behind the ledger-alb load balancer. After a rollout the ALB reports every target as unreachable. Someone opened port 8080 on ledger-api-sg because "APIs usually listen on 8080", but the platform team records the real listening port of each service in Parameter Store, under /ledger/api/listen-port.
mission.objective: Make ledger-api-sg accept traffic on the port the service really listens on, only from the ledger-alb-sg load balancer group (not from CIDR ranges), and remove the stale 8080 opening.

mission.name: The Office Moved
mission.description: Northwind Logistics' engineers work from one office and reach the build bastion over SSH. The company moved buildings last month and the engineers have not been able to connect since. The new office's public egress range is 203.0.113.0/24. The security group nw-bastion-sg still carries a rule somebody typed for the old building.
mission.objective: Allow SSH to the bastion from the new office range 203.0.113.0/24 only. The old rule must not linger, and SSH must never be opened to the whole internet.

mission.name: Hardened Into a Corner
mission.description: Parcelwise's route-optimizer worker was "hardened" by the security team: its default allow-all outbound rule was removed from parcel-worker-sg and nothing was put in its place. Since then the worker cannot call the carrier tracking API over HTTPS and cannot reach its PostgreSQL database (parcel-db-sg already admits the worker on port 5432). Security wants the group to stay locked down to what the worker actually uses.
mission.objective: Give parcel-worker-sg outbound access to HTTPS (443) on the internet and to PostgreSQL (5432) on the parcel-db-sg group, and nothing broader than that.

mission.name: Room for Meridian
mission.description: Meridian Health is standing up its production network. An engineer already created a VPC called meridian-prod in a hurry, but the networking review rejected it: it uses the same address space as the shared-services VPC that Meridian will peer with later, and DNS hostnames are off, which the Kubernetes team needs. VPC address ranges cannot be changed once the VPC exists.
mission.objective: Make exactly one VPC named meridian-prod (Name tag) exist, with an IPv4 CIDR from the 10.0.0.0/8 private range, size between /16 and /20, that overlaps neither shared-services nor the default VPC, and with DNS hostnames enabled.

mission.name: An ALB With Nowhere to Land
mission.description: Brightwave Media's platform team created the brightwave-prod VPC (10.70.0.0/16) and handed it to the web team, who immediately tried to create an Application Load Balancer in it. The VPC has no subnets yet, and Brightwave requires every public load balancer to survive the loss of an availability zone.
mission.objective: Build the public tier: at least two subnets in brightwave-prod, each in a different availability zone, each tagged Tier=public, with non-overlapping CIDRs inside the VPC range, no smaller than a /26 each. An Application Load Balancer must be creatable across them.

mission.name: Skyline Café Is Offline
mission.description: Skyline Café's online ordering site runs on one instance in the skyline-prod VPC's public subnet. It has a public IP and a permissive security group, and the subnet's route table even has a default route. Still, customers cannot load the page and the instance cannot reach the internet. There are two internet gateways in the account: skyline-igw, built for this VPC, and an old legacy-igw from a decommissioned project.
mission.objective: Restore internet access for the skyline-prod public subnet: the default route of its route table must lead to an internet gateway that is actually attached to skyline-prod. Keep using skyline-igw and do not touch the instance.

mission.name: Dead End Street
mission.description: Harborview Dental's booking site lives in the harborview-prod VPC. The VPC has an attached internet gateway, a web subnet and a private db subnet, but both subnets use the VPC's automatically created main route table, which only has the local route. Patients get timeouts and the web server cannot reach the appointment-reminder API. The database subnet must never become reachable from the internet.
mission.objective: Make the web subnet public (default route to the internet gateway) while the db subnet stays private (no route to any internet gateway).

mission.name: Wired to the Wrong Subnet
mission.description: Fernhill Games' matchmaking service runs on instances in fh-app (public) and keeps its database in fh-data (private). The fernhill-public route table has a perfectly good default route to the internet gateway, and the matchmaking servers still cannot get out. Meanwhile the security scanner just reported that something in the data subnet is exposed.
mission.objective: Put the internet route where it belongs: the fh-app subnet must use the fernhill-public route table, and fh-data must have no route to an internet gateway. Keep the fernhill-public table and its route.

mission.name: The Rule Before the Rule
mission.description: Lumen Tickets' box-office site runs in the lumen-prod VPC behind the lumen-web-nacl network ACL. After an abuse incident the security team added rules to that NACL, and since then visitors get timeouts on port 80 although the security group allows it and HTTPS still works. The abuse range 198.51.100.0/24 must remain blocked, and the NACL must keep working as a stateless filter.
mission.objective: Let the internet reach the web subnet on HTTP (80) and HTTPS (443) through lumen-web-nacl, keep 198.51.100.0/24 blocked, keep replies able to leave (ephemeral ports), and do not expose any other port. The subnet must stay associated with lumen-web-nacl.

mission.name: Born Without Credentials
mission.description: Ember Analytics' ember-api instance is supposed to read its configuration from s3://ember-config at startup. The platform team prepared an IAM role called ember-app-role with the right S3 permissions and told the application team "the instance can use it". The app still logs "Unable to locate credentials", and the security review noted that the role could not be used by EC2 even if it were attached.
mission.objective: Make the running ember-api instance able to use ember-app-role: the instance needs an instance profile containing the role, and EC2 must be allowed to assume it. The role may read objects in s3://ember-config only (no write access, no other buckets).

mission.name: No Key, No Entry
mission.description: Atlas Robotics' on-call engineers need to SSH into the atlas-bastion host in the public subnet. The instance was launched from the console without choosing a key pair, and the team's shared key pair platform-ops already exists in the account. Engineers get "Permission denied (publickey)". A key pair can only be chosen when an instance is launched; there is no command to add one to a running instance.
mission.objective: Replace the keyless bastion with one that boots with the existing platform-ops key pair: in the same subnet (atlas-public) and security group (atlas-bastion-sg), same Name tag atlas-bastion. Exactly one atlas-bastion may be left running, and the keyless one must be terminated.

mission.name: Invisible Instance
mission.description: Orbit Telecom hosts its public status page on the orbit-status instance in the orbit-prod public subnet. Routing, the internet gateway and the security group have all been reviewed and are correct, yet the page is unreachable: the instance only has a private address. A partner firewall allow-lists the status page's IP, so whatever address it gets must stay the same across stop/start cycles.
mission.objective: Give the running orbit-status instance a public IPv4 address that is stable across restarts. Do not replace the instance.

mission.name: Gossip Behind Closed Doors
mission.description: Cobalt Cache runs a three-node membership cluster whose nodes gossip with each other on TCP and UDP 7946. The nodes are healthy individually, yet they never form a cluster: each one reports "no peers found". They all share the security group cobalt-nodes-sg, which only has a rule admitting the monitoring server. Cobalt security forbids opening cluster ports to CIDR ranges, because nodes are replaced all the time and their addresses change.
mission.objective: Let the members of cobalt-nodes-sg talk to each other on TCP and UDP 7946, without allowing that traffic from any address range and without opening any further port. The monitoring rule must stay.

mission.name: Peering Without a Path
mission.description: Two teams at Copperline Retail own separate VPCs: orders-vpc (10.160.0.0/16) and billing-vpc (10.161.0.0/16). Yesterday someone requested a peering connection between them so the order service can call the billing database on port 5432. The request was made and then everybody went home. The order service still cannot connect, and the billing team says their database never even sees a packet.
mission.objective: Make the peering usable in both directions: the connection must be active, each VPC's private route table must route the other VPC's CIDR through it, and the billing database group must accept PostgreSQL only from the orders VPC range. Do not route 0.0.0.0/0 over the peering.

mission.name: Private Road to S3
mission.description: Quartz Data runs nightly exports from quartz-batch in a private subnet that deliberately has no route to the internet. The job writes to the bucket quartz-exports and now hangs on every upload. Management refuses to add a NAT gateway ("we pay for that per hour and per GB"), and compliance demands that the private path to S3 can only reach the company's own bucket.
mission.objective: Give the private subnet a private path to S3 with a VPC gateway endpoint: it must serve com.amazonaws.us-east-1.s3, be attached to the private route table only (not the public one), and its endpoint policy may only allow access to quartz-exports. The private route table must still have no internet route.

mission.name: Parse Error
mission.description: Harbor Lights Ferry is moving its passenger-info plumbing into CloudFormation. Priya, the new platform engineer, wrote template.yaml for the timetable bucket and the delay-alert topic, but the very first deploy dies before a single resource is created. The CLI only prints a terse "Template format error" and Priya has already stared at the file for an hour.
mission.objective: Deploy template.yaml as a stack named harborlights-core and get it to CREATE_COMPLETE, with the versioned timetable bucket and the delay-alert topic both really present.

mission.name: Green Stack, Missing Bucket
mission.description: Brightwater Dental scans every new-patient form into a bucket that the brightwater-intake stack is supposed to own. The deploy pipeline reports a green CREATE_COMPLETE and the reminder topic is there, yet the front-desk app fails every upload with NoSuchBucket. Somebody hand-typed the intake template last Friday.
mission.objective: Repair the brightwater-intake stack so that the scanned-forms bucket brightwater-scans really exists and accepts uploads, while the stack stays healthy and keeps its reminder topic.

mission.name: Nobody Can Wear This Role
mission.description: Lumen Labs' nightly job exports lab results by signing in as the IAM user export-runner and assuming the role lumen-exporter, which is created by the lumen-export stack. The stack deployed without a single error, but every night the job dies on its very first call with an AccessDenied from sts:AssumeRole. The permissions on the role look fine.
mission.objective: Fix the lumen-export stack so that export-runner can assume lumen-exporter and upload results to the lumen-lab-exports bucket. No other principal may be able to assume the role, and the role must still be unable to write to anything but that bucket.

mission.name: Who Fills the Blank?
mission.description: Fernwood Bakery's online-order system keeps each shop's orders in its own bucket, named after the shop's branch code. The platform team's template takes the branch code as a parameter, and the intern's deploy script simply runs create-stack with the template and nothing else. The command is rejected before anything is created, and the error mentions "must have values".
mission.objective: Deploy the template as a stack named fernwood-orders for the branch code "dub" so that the orders bucket exists and is named for the branch, with a non-empty branch code (an anonymous bucket named only "fernwood-orders-" is not acceptable).

mission.name: Thirty Seconds, Give or Take an S
mission.description: Quarry Photo Co. resizes customer uploads in a Lambda function deployed by the quarry-resizer stack. Large panoramas need a 45 second timeout, so the release engineer put "45s" into the parameter file that the deploy script feeds to create-stack. The stack went to ROLLBACK_COMPLETE and the function was never created. The retry button in the pipeline just fails the same way.
mission.objective: Get the quarry-resizer stack to CREATE_COMPLETE with the Lambda function quarry-resizer configured with a 45 second timeout, passing the value through the template's own TimeoutSeconds parameter.

mission.name: Ref to Nowhere
mission.description: Tidewater Logistics' dispatch app does not hard-code bucket names. It reads the SSM parameter /tidewater/manifest-bucket at startup and writes the daily shipping manifests into whatever bucket that parameter names. Since the tidewater-manifests stack was deployed, the dispatch app has been failing with NoSuchBucket, even though the stack is CREATE_COMPLETE and the manifest bucket is sitting right there.
mission.objective: Fix the tidewater-manifests stack so that the app's parameter /tidewater/manifest-bucket names the stack's real manifest bucket, and a manifest can be written to the bucket that the parameter points at.

mission.name: Attribute Not Found
mission.description: Orchard Analytics is rolling out release 2 of its orchard-reporting stack: a new archive bucket, and permission for the reporting role to copy finished reports into it. The workspace holds the release template. Rolling it out with update-stack makes the update fail and roll back, which leaves the archive bucket missing and the reporting bot unable to archive anything.
mission.objective: Roll out release 2: update the orchard-reporting stack so that report-bot, by assuming the role orchard-reporter, can upload to both orchard-reports and the new orchard-archive bucket and nowhere else, with the stack ending in UPDATE_COMPLETE.

mission.name: Chicken, Egg, Bucket
mission.description: Granite Peak Media wants every file dropped into its upload bucket to announce itself on an SNS topic. The topic needs a policy that lets only that bucket publish, and S3 insists the policy exist before the bucket's notification is wired up. The platform engineer encoded exactly that in template.yaml, but create-stack refuses to start and complains about a circular dependency.
mission.objective: Deploy the template as the stack granitepeak-intake so that a file uploaded to granitepeak-uploads produces a notification on the topic granitepeak-upload-events, and the topic's publish permission is still restricted to that bucket.
concepts: implicit dependencies via GetAtt and Ref

mission.name: Stack Stuck in Rollback
mission.description: Saltmarsh Pharmacy's release train deployed the saltmarsh-api stack a few minutes before the saltmarsh-shared stack it depends on. The api stack died on creation and has been sitting in ROLLBACK_COMPLETE ever since. The shared stack has meanwhile been deployed successfully, but re-running the api deploy as an update is refused with an error about the stack state.
mission.objective: Get saltmarsh-api to CREATE_COMPLETE with its template unchanged, so that the SSM parameter /saltmarsh/alerts-topic holds the topic ARN exported by saltmarsh-shared. The shared stack must be left alone.

mission.name: Name Taken
mission.description: Quayside Ferries' web team already consumes the export quayside-assets-bucket from the quayside-network stack. Now the reporting team has copied that stack's template as the starting point for their own, quayside-reports, and the deploy fails with CREATE_FAILED and a complaint about an export that is "already exported by another stack". The existing web stack must keep working untouched while the reporting team gets their bucket.
mission.objective: Deploy the reporting template as the stack quayside-reports so that it exports its own bucket name under a name of its own, while the existing quayside-assets-bucket export and the quayside-web stack that imports it keep their original values.

mission.name: No Export Named That
mission.description: Ledgerline's compliance team wants an auditor stack that records where the production audit topic and audit bucket live, so scanners can look them up in SSM. The auditor template pulls both values from the platform stacks with ImportValue, but the first deploy attempt rolls back with "No export named ... found". Two platform stacks (production and staging) publish similarly named exports, so it is easy to grab the wrong one.
mission.objective: Deploy the auditor template as the stack ledgerline-auditor so that the SSM parameters /ledgerline/audit/topic-arn and /ledgerline/audit/bucket hold the PRODUCTION audit topic ARN and bucket name, as exported by the production platform stack.

mission.name: Upside-Down Production
mission.description: Marlow Books runs one catalog template for every environment. After last week's refactor the production catalog bucket stopped keeping object versions, the on-call pager topic is missing from production, and a noisy debug topic meant for developer sandboxes has shown up there instead. The production stack marlow-catalog was deployed with Environment=prod and the parameters look right.
mission.objective: Repair the marlow-catalog stack (keeping Environment=prod) so production has a versioned catalog bucket and the pager topic and no debug topic, while the same template still behaves as a developer sandbox when deployed with Environment=dev (debug topic, no pager).

mission.name: Handle With Care
mission.description: Nightjar Finance is retiring the nightjar-archive stack: it was a pilot, and the team wants CloudFormation out of the picture. The stack, however, owns the ledger archive bucket and the ledger index table, both full of records the auditors will ask for next year. Only the small events topic is disposable. A colleague once ran delete-stack on a sibling stack "to see what happens" and the table went with it.
mission.objective: Retire the nightjar-archive stack completely (it must be gone, and the events topic with it) while the ledger archive bucket and the ledger index table survive with every record intact.

mission.name: Policy Lock
mission.description: Kestrel Robotics spins up one CloudFormation stack per pull request so reviewers get a live preview. Last quarter an engineer deleted production by mistake, so the shared deploy wrapper now switches on termination protection for every stack it creates, previews included. The nightly cleanup job has been failing ever since: the stack for the merged PR #731 refuses to go away and its bucket and topic keep costing money. PR #742 is still under review and production runs in kestrel-prod-core.
mission.objective: Remove the preview stack kestrel-pr-731 and its resources, while kestrel-pr-742 and kestrel-prod-core stay deployed and keep their termination protection.

mission.name: Missing Map Entry
mission.description: Cobalt Telehealth sizes its appointment-reminder Lambda per region from a Mappings table: bigger memory where call volume is high, smaller elsewhere. The capacity plan says the primary region, us-east-1, gets 1024 MB and a 20 second timeout. A new engineer deployed the stack in us-east-1 and it rolled back; the events mention the Lambda function failing to create with an odd, empty-looking value. Nobody edited the function itself.
mission.objective: Deploy the stack cobalt-reminders in us-east-1 so that the Lambda function cobalt-reminder-sender runs with 1024 MB and a 20 second timeout, with the sizing still coming from the template's Mappings table rather than being hard-coded.

mission.name: SAM Template Rejected
mission.description: Parcelhub's courier team writes its notifier Lambda with the AWS Serverless Application Model (SAM) shorthand: a single AWS::Serverless::Function instead of a function, a role and an alias spelled out by hand. They deploy template.yaml as the stack parcelhub-notifier. CloudFormation answers with a perfectly green status, yet there is no Lambda function anywhere in the account, and the dispatch system gets "function not found" when it tries to call parcel-notifier.
mission.objective: Deploy template.yaml as the stack parcelhub-notifier so that the Lambda function parcel-notifier really exists and answers an invocation with the stage name from its environment.

mission.name: Reality Diverged
mission.description: At 2 a.m. the on-call engineer at Tern Streaming rescued a flooded ingest pipeline by hand: she raised the Lambda tern-ingest-fn from 128 MB / 3 s to 512 MB / 30 s, tripled its batch size, and switched on versioning on the landing bucket. It worked, nobody touched CloudFormation, and the incident was closed. The tern-ingest stack's template still describes the old settings, so the next routine deploy could quietly undo the fix. This emulator has no drift-detection API, so you will have to compare reality and the template yourself.
mission.objective: Bring the tern-ingest stack's template in line with what is really running (template.json in your workspace is the stack's current template), without reverting any of the on-call engineer's changes. Afterwards no property in the stack's template may disagree with the live Lambda function and bucket.

mission.name: Nested Stack 404
mission.description: Crescent Payments splits its platform into a parent stack and reusable child templates stored in the S3 bucket crescent-templates. The parent stack crescent-platform nests an "alerts" child that creates the billing team's alert topic and hands its ARN back to the parent as an output, which the on-call dashboard reads. The pipeline's first run left crescent-platform in a failed state with an S3 "does not exist" complaint. The author suspects the URL is not the only thing wrong with the parent.
mission.objective: Get crescent-platform to CREATE_COMPLETE with the child stack really created from the template stored in crescent-templates, and make the parent's AlertsTopicArn output carry the ARN of the topic the child created.

mission.name: No Key
mission.description: Lanternfish Labs' document vault seals every uploaded contract with KMS before storing it. The vault is configured to use the key alias alias/lanternfish-vault, which was supposed to be created by the platform team during the migration but never was. Since go-live every upload fails with a NotFoundException saying the alias is not found. Security has added one requirement: the key must rotate automatically every year.
mission.objective: Provide the vault with what it expects: a customer-managed symmetric encryption key reachable as alias/lanternfish-vault, enabled, with automatic key rotation turned on, so that data can be encrypted and decrypted through the alias.

mission.name: Disabled Key
mission.description: Marigold Pay tokenises card numbers: the token service stores each token as KMS ciphertext in SSM parameters under /marigold/tokens/ and decrypts it on demand through the alias alias/marigold-tokens. Overnight a "key hygiene" script flagged the key as unused and switched it off. Since the morning rush every checkout fails with a DisabledException. Re-encrypting the tokens with a different key is not possible: the original card data is not stored anywhere.
mission.objective: Make the stored tokens under /marigold/tokens/ decryptable again, so that the token service gets the original token values back through KMS.

mission.name: No Key Permission
mission.description: Orbit Health encrypts patient reports with the KMS key alias/orbit-reports. The reporting service runs as the IAM role orbit-report-writer, whose own IAM policy already lists the KMS actions it needs. Yet the security audit shows the writer would be refused by KMS: when the key was re-created last month someone pasted in a key policy that only names the key administrator, key-admin, and has no statement for anyone else. A KMS key policy is the first thing KMS consults, and IAM policies alone cannot override it.
mission.objective: Replace the key policy of alias/orbit-reports (key-policy.json in your workspace holds the current one) so that orbit-report-writer may use the key to encrypt and decrypt data, while key-admin keeps administering it. Do not open the key to everyone or hand the writer administrative control.

mission.name: Wrong Key Name
mission.description: The Ironbridge Outfitters orders service encrypts customer records with the alias alias/orders-prod. Support noticed that new production records land encrypted under the staging key: the compliance team's audit script, which is only allowed to read the production key, cannot decrypt anything written since Tuesday's "alias tidy-up". Old records, written before that, are fine. Nobody remembers which key the alias used to point at, and key IDs are not very memorable.
mission.objective: Make alias/orders-prod resolve to the production orders key again (the key that decrypts the existing production records) without disturbing alias/orders-staging or the staging key.

mission.name: No Secret
mission.description: Wyvern Games' matchmaking service fetches its database credentials from the Secrets Manager secret wyvern/matchmaker/db-credentials when it starts. This morning every matchmaker instance failed its health check. The error is not the usual "secret not found": Secrets Manager says it cannot perform the operation on a secret that was marked for deletion. A tidy-up script ran last night, and the database password only exists inside that secret.
mission.objective: Get wyvern/matchmaker/db-credentials readable again with its original contents (same password, username and host), without creating a replacement secret.

mission.name: Wrong Key in JSON
mission.description: Cinder Analytics keeps its warehouse login in the secret cinder/warehouse/login. The new BI dashboard reads the JSON fields "user" and "pass", but the secret was created in the standard database layout with "username" and "password", so the dashboard logs "KeyError: 'user'" and shows nothing. The nightly billing job, written years ago, reads "username" and "password" and works perfectly; it must keep working. The secret.json file in your workspace holds the current contents.
mission.objective: Make cinder/warehouse/login satisfy both consumers: the dashboard must find user and pass with the real credentials, while the billing job must still find username and password, as well as host and port. Keep the history, so the previous version stays available as AWSPREVIOUS.

mission.name: Access Denied to Secret
mission.description: Quokka Pay's payments API runs as the IAM role quokka-api and loads its processor token from the secret quokka/prod/payments-api at startup. After Monday's deploy the service crash-loops with AccessDeniedException on GetSecretValue. The secret exists and its value is fine; the role's inline policy quokka-secrets was edited in the same release, and policy.json in your workspace is the copy that was applied.
mission.objective: Let quokka-api read quokka/prod/payments-api, and only that secret. It must stay unable to read the admin console secret (quokka/prod/admin-console) or the staging secret.

mission.name: Wrong Version
mission.description: Sable Streaming rotates the CDN URL-signing key stored in the secret sable/cdn/signing-key by hand. On Thursday the new key was stored, and the edge servers (which always fetch the default version of the secret) signed URLs with it. A runbook step then "rolled back" something in the secret, and since then the edge fleet signs URLs with the retired key, which the CDN origin refuses. The new key is still in the secret; nobody deleted anything.
mission.objective: Make the new signing key (the one stored in the newer version of sable/cdn/signing-key) the default value again, keeping the retired key available as AWSPREVIOUS for the 24-hour overlap period.

mission.name: Stale Credentials
mission.description: Pelican Freight's orders database password lives in the secret pelican/orders-db/password and is supposed to rotate automatically. The audit team noticed the "last rotated" date is months old and the console shows rotation pointing at a Lambda function that no longer exists: the old rotator (v1) was decommissioned when the platform team shipped its replacement, and nobody reconfigured the secret. Company policy says database passwords must rotate at least every 30 days.
mission.objective: Reconfigure rotation of pelican/orders-db/password so that it uses the rotation function that is actually deployed for the orders database, rotating automatically at least every 30 days.

mission.name: Missing Config
mission.description: Corvid Commerce's checkout service no longer has connection settings baked into its image: at startup it reads /corvid/checkout/db-host and /corvid/checkout/db-port from SSM Parameter Store, running as the IAM role corvid-checkout. The new environment was provisioned in a hurry and the service dies with ParameterNotFound. The role's permissions have already been set up for the /corvid/checkout/ path. The database's connection details are recorded in the secret corvid/checkout/db-credentials.
mission.objective: Create the two parameters the service reads, /corvid/checkout/db-host and /corvid/checkout/db-port, holding the host and port recorded for the checkout database, so that the corvid-checkout role can read both.

mission.name: Plaintext Secret
mission.description: A Harrier Pay security scan flagged the Parameter Store entry /harrier/payments/api-key: the card processor's live API key is stored as a plain String, readable in clear text by anyone who can call ssm:GetParameter, and it appears in console screenshots. The team has its own customer-managed key for configuration secrets, alias/harrier-config. The sibling parameter /harrier/payments/timeout-ms is harmless and is read by a legacy tool that cannot decrypt anything.
mission.objective: Store /harrier/payments/api-key as an encrypted SecureString under the key alias/harrier-config, keeping its value (the service must not need a new key), and leave /harrier/payments/timeout-ms as an ordinary String.

mission.name: Path Confusion
mission.description: Lattice Labs' inventory service reads its configuration from Parameter Store at boot: /lattice/production/db-host, /lattice/production/db-user and /lattice/production/db-password, running as the IAM user lattice-svc. It crashes with ParameterNotFound on the very first one. The configuration was provisioned by a script that wrote it under /lattice/prod instead. Other teams' dashboards already read /lattice/prod, and the service's IAM policy deliberately allows only the production subtree.
mission.objective: Make the three parameters readable at the paths the service uses, as lattice-svc, with the same values as in /lattice/prod and the password still stored encrypted (SecureString). lattice-svc must remain unable to read anything under /lattice/prod, and the old parameters must stay in place.

mission.name: SSM Blocked
mission.description: Kiln Games' matchmaking workers run as ECS tasks with the IAM role kiln-task. At startup each task reads two parameters: the queue URL /kiln/prod/queue-url (a plain String) and the database password /kiln/prod/db-password (a SecureString encrypted with the customer-managed key alias/kiln-config). Since the infrastructure refactor every task exits within seconds, logging AccessDeniedException from SSM. policy.json in your workspace is the inline policy that was applied to the role.
mission.objective: Fix the role's inline policy kiln-task-config so that kiln-task can read both production parameters, including decrypting the SecureString with its key, while still being unable to read /kiln/dev/..., /kiln-admin/... or to decrypt with other keys.

mission.name: Rotation Breaks Decrypt
mission.description: Atlas Records "rotated" its archive encryption key the manual way: the platform team created a new key, pointed alias/atlas-data at it, and then disabled the old key as the runbook says. New writes work, but the archive reader, which decrypts ciphertext stored in /atlas/archive/record-1 to record-3 without naming any key, now fails on every old record with a DisabledException. The records were encrypted with the encryption context dataset=atlas-archive. Leaving the old key enabled forever defeats the point of rotating, and a repeat of this exercise next year is not acceptable.
mission.objective: Migrate the three archive records so they are encrypted under the key behind alias/atlas-data (keeping their encryption context and plaintext), leave the old key disabled but not deleted, and enable automatic key rotation on the current key so that future rotations never need this migration.

mission.name: Credentials in Code
mission.description: A code review at Nimbus Metrics found that the Lambda function nimbus-exporter carries a long-lived IAM access key in its environment variables (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, belonging to the CI user nimbus-ci) so that it can read its API token from Secrets Manager. The function's actual execution role, nimbus-bare, has no permissions. The key has been visible to everyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration since March. The function also needs two settings, APP_ENV and TOKEN_SECRET_ID, that must keep working.
mission.objective: Make nimbus-exporter authenticate through its execution role instead: remove the embedded keys (keeping its other settings), give it a role that trusts Lambda and may read only the secret nimbus/exporter/api-token, and take the leaked access key out of circulation.

mission.name: The Cluster That Never Was
mission.description: Ledgerly's finance team runs a nightly ledger report as an ECS Fargate task. The task definition nightly-report is registered, and run-report.sh has worked for months, but this morning it prints an error and no report was produced. A migration script that "tidied up old clusters" ran last night.
mission.objective: Get the nightly-report task running again on the ECS cluster named ledgerly-batch, using the registered task definition.

mission.name: Deployed Nothing
mission.description: Harbor Freight Tracker's web frontend is deployed with deploy.sh, which creates the ECS service harbor-web in the harbor cluster from task definition harbor-web:1. Since the account was reorganised the script fails right away. The container spec is kept in harbor-web.json in the repo, but nobody is sure it was ever registered in this account.
mission.objective: Get the harbor-web service running with two healthy tasks (desired = running = 2) that answer HTTP on port 80.

mission.name: Sizing the Thumbnailer
mission.description: Snapwell's image thumbnailer is a memory-hungry Fargate task: its container needs a hard limit of 1536 MiB. The engineer who wrote task-definition.json guessed the sizes and now registering it fails with "No Fargate configuration exists for given values". Fargate only offers specific CPU and memory pairs, and finance does not want anything bigger than necessary.
mission.objective: Register a task definition for the family thumbnailer that is a valid Fargate size, has enough task memory for the container's 1536 MiB hard limit, and does not exceed 1 vCPU or 4 GiB. A task from it must actually start.

mission.name: Nobody to Pull the Secret
mission.description: PayrollWorks is shipping revision 2 of its payroll-api service, which reads the database password from Secrets Manager (payroll/db-password) and logs to CloudWatch. The release pipeline's pre-flight check refuses to promote the task definition. On real Fargate this revision would die at start-up with "ResourceInitializationError: unable to pull secrets". The definition in task-definition.json names no execution role at all, and no suitable role exists in the account.
mission.objective: Ship payroll-api with a proper ECS task execution role: create it, make sure it can read payroll/db-password (and no other secret), write to the payroll-api log group and authenticate to the container registry, reference it from a new task definition revision, and roll the payroll-api service onto that revision.

mission.name: Access Denied at the Bucket
mission.description: Pixelmill's resizer service reads uploaded photos from pixelmill-uploads and writes thumbnails to pixelmill-thumbs. Its ECS task role, pixelmill-task-role, has a policy that "mentions the right buckets", yet the application logs AccessDenied on every GetObject and PutObject. Pixelmill also stores invoices in pixelmill-billing, which the resizer must never touch.
mission.objective: Fix the permissions of pixelmill-task-role so the resizer can read objects from pixelmill-uploads, list that bucket and write objects to pixelmill-thumbs, with nothing else allowed (no writes to uploads, no deletes, no other buckets). The resizer service must keep running with that role.

mission.name: The Image That Wasn't There
mission.description: Hearthstone Pantry's storefront task stops within a second of being launched by deploy.sh; the container never starts. The release pipeline publishes the approved image reference for the storefront into Parameter Store at /hearth/web/approved-image after every build, but task-definition.json was last edited by hand during an incident.
mission.objective: Get a hearth-web task running that uses exactly the image the release pipeline approved (the value of /hearth/web/approved-image), and serving HTTP on port 80.

mission.name: Knocking on the Wrong Door
mission.description: Invoicely's invoice-api runs on Fargate behind the target group invoice-tg (port 3000, health check GET /health). Every target stays unhealthy and the load balancer returns errors. The application team swears the service listens on port 3000, but the task definition they copied from another service declares container port 8080, and the ECS service registers that port with the target group.
mission.objective: Get invoice-api's targets healthy in invoice-tg: the task definition and the service's load-balancer mapping must use the port the application actually listens on. Keep the target group as it is.

mission.name: Paused for Maintenance, Never Resumed
mission.description: Sundial Scheduling's booking API is the ECS service sundial-api in the sundial cluster. Last Friday an engineer scaled it to zero for a database maintenance window and went on holiday. The service shows ACTIVE and green in the console, yet customers get 503 from the load balancer. The runbook says production keeps two tasks, so a rolling deploy never drops to zero capacity.
mission.objective: Bring sundial-api back with two running tasks (desired = running = 2) serving HTTP on port 80, without changing its task definition.

mission.name: Crash on Arrival
mission.description: Pulse Metrics' ingest worker (ECS service pulse-ingest, a queue consumer, not an HTTP API) keeps starting and dying. The service always shows desired 1, running 0, and a growing list of stopped tasks. The container exits within a second of starting. The application's start-up script validates its environment; its output goes to the CloudWatch log group /ecs/pulse-ingest.
mission.objective: Make pulse-ingest stay up: find out why the container exits, fix the configuration in a new task definition revision, and roll the service onto it. The worker must run in the mode that fits a queue consumer.

mission.name: Secret Handshake Failed
mission.description: Cedar Bank's ledger-sync service pulls its database credentials from Secrets Manager at start-up. After a secret was renamed during a tidy-up, new tasks of ledger-sync never start: ECS marks them stopped within seconds, before the application code runs. Nobody remembers the exact new ARN, and the person who edited task-definition.json typed it from memory.
mission.objective: Make ledger-sync run again with the container receiving DB_USER and DB_PASSWORD from the secret cedar/db-credentials (keys username and password): register a corrected task definition and roll the service onto it.

mission.name: Permanently Unhealthy
mission.description: Tidewater Pay's gateway service runs on Fargate behind the target group gateway-tg. The tasks start and stay running, the port is right, but the load balancer marks every target unhealthy and would take the whole service out of rotation. The gateway answers 200 on its own readiness endpoint /health; every other path, including /, is not part of the API contract.
mission.objective: Make gateway-tg report the gateway's targets healthy by fixing the target group's health check to probe the real endpoint with the strict success code 200. Do not widen the accepted response codes, and do not change the application.

mission.name: Silent Checkout
mission.description: Marigold Market's checkout-worker has been running fine for weeks, but the on-call dashboard that reads the CloudWatch log group /ecs/checkout-worker has been empty ever since the service moved to Fargate. The task definition revision 1 configures the container's logs with the journald logging driver, copied from the old EC2 setup. Fargate only ships logs through supported drivers such as awslogs. The log group already exists and has a 14-day retention that must be kept.
mission.objective: Make checkout-worker's logs arrive in the existing /ecs/checkout-worker log group: register a corrected task definition revision using the awslogs driver and roll the service onto it. The log group (and its retention) must not be recreated.

mission.name: Private but Stranded
mission.description: Lantern Analytics runs its lantern-sync Fargate service in a private subnet (lantern-private) so that it is never reachable from the internet. The service must call a partner's HTTPS API, and pulls images from a public registry. Since the move into the private subnet the task cannot reach anything outside the VPC (image pulls and API calls time out). The VPC has a public subnet (lantern-public) with an internet gateway, and nothing else.
mission.objective: Give lantern-private outbound-only internet access: create a NAT gateway in the public subnet with an Elastic IP and route the private subnet's default route to it. The private subnet must still have no direct route to the internet gateway.

mission.name: Locked Out of Our Own Endpoints
mission.description: Slate Reports runs its slate-reports Fargate service in an isolated VPC with no internet route at all. It reaches AWS through interface VPC endpoints for ECR, CloudWatch Logs and Secrets Manager, protected by the security group slate-vpce-sg. The task group slate-task-sg was hardened to have no outbound rules, and slate-vpce-sg still trusts the CIDR of a subnet that was deleted a year ago. New tasks cannot pull images or log, and nothing in the VPC can use the endpoints.
mission.objective: Open exactly the path tasks need to reach the endpoints: slate-task-sg may send HTTPS (443) to slate-vpce-sg, and slate-vpce-sg must accept HTTPS from slate-task-sg. No rule may use 0.0.0.0/0, and the task group must not become allow-all.
concepts: security group egress and ingress pairing

mission.name: Who Is inventory.shop.local?
mission.description: Bramble Shop's catalog service looks up the inventory service by the DNS name inventory.shop.local, a convention every team agreed on. Two ECS services exist (catalog and inventory) but the lookup fails: there is no shop.local namespace and the inventory tasks are not registered anywhere. The inventory service runs two tasks, whose IP addresses change at every deployment, so hard-coding them is not an option.
mission.objective: Set up AWS Cloud Map service discovery so that the name inventory.shop.local resolves to the live inventory tasks: a private DNS namespace shop.local, a service named inventory with A records, and the ECS inventory service registered to it. Every running inventory task must be listed with its real IP.

mission.name: Friday Deploy Gone Wrong
mission.description: Tidepool Travel deployed revision 2 of its web service at 16:45 on a Friday. Revision 1 served customers fine. Revision 2 crashes during start-up (its new database migration step fails and exits), and because the deploy had no protection the service replaced healthy capacity with tasks that die. The page is down and the rollout is stuck. The team also wants this never to happen silently again.
mission.objective: Restore service quickly: tidepool-web must run two healthy tasks on the last good revision (revision 1, or a newer revision that really works) answering HTTP on port 80. Then protect future deployments by enabling the ECS deployment circuit breaker with automatic rollback on the service.

mission.name: Status Page With No Page
mission.description: Lantern runs a public status page. Its front end calls GET /status on the REST API lantern-status-api and shows the "state" field. The Lambda function that knows the state, lantern-status, was deployed yesterday, but the API in front of it never existed: the Terraform apply that should have created it was cancelled halfway. Browsers get nothing but errors and the support inbox is filling up with "is Lantern down?" mails. The function already speaks the Lambda proxy format, so it needs no changes.
mission.objective: Build the REST API lantern-status-api so that GET /status on the stage live returns the status JSON produced by the lantern-status function, through a Lambda proxy integration.

mission.name: Notes Without an Address
mission.description: Quillnote is a note-taking app. Its REST API quillnote-api (stage v1) serves GET /notes just fine, and a new mobile build now opens a single note with GET /notes/{noteId}, for example /notes/n-204. Every one of those calls fails while the list screen works. The Lambda behind the API, quillnote-notes, already handles both shapes of request: it reads the note id from the path parameter noteId and returns 400 when it is missing. The API definition was written by hand and nobody added the second route.
mission.objective: Make GET /notes/{noteId} on stage v1 of quillnote-api return the requested note through the quillnote-notes function, while GET /notes keeps working. The function must receive the id as the path parameter noteId.

mission.name: Read-Only by Accident
mission.description: Parcelpoint's help desk widget lets customers file a ticket by POSTing JSON to /tickets on the REST API parcelpoint-help (stage prod), and lists existing tickets with GET /tickets. Listing works. Filing a ticket doesn't: the widget gets HTTP 403 with "Missing Authentication Token" even though nobody asked for authentication. Two Lambda functions exist, parcelpoint-ticket-list and parcelpoint-ticket-create; only the first is attached to the API. The create function expects a JSON body with a title and answers 201.
mission.objective: Make POST /tickets on stage prod of parcelpoint-help create a ticket through parcelpoint-ticket-create (HTTP 201 with the new ticket echoed back), without breaking GET /tickets, which must keep using the list function.

mission.name: A Door Into an Empty Room
mission.description: Brewbook is a coffee-roaster catalogue. The search box calls GET /brews?roast=dark on the REST API brewbook-api (stage test). The route exists, the method is open, and the request is accepted, but nothing useful ever comes back: the app shows an empty page or an error. The search logic lives in the Lambda function brewbook-search, which reads the roast from the query string and returns the matching brews as JSON. Someone built the API method by hand and called it a day.
mission.objective: Connect GET /brews on stage test of brewbook-api to the brewbook-search function so that /brews?roast=dark returns the dark roasts and /brews?roast=light the light ones.

mission.name: Dial the Right Number
mission.description: Invoicely's customer portal downloads the latest invoice via GET /invoices/latest on the REST API invoicely-portal (stage prod). Since yesterday's rename of the rendering function the portal shows "Something went wrong". Two functions with similar names live in the account: invoice-renderer (production) and invoice-renderer-staging (the sandbox finance uses for new templates). API Gateway is wired to a function ARN that somebody typed by hand. Real customers must get production invoices, and finance's staging sandbox must stay out of the customer path.
mission.objective: Repair the integration of GET /invoices/latest on invoicely-portal so that it invokes the production function invoice-renderer and the portal receives its invoice again.

mission.name: Locked Out After the Rebuild
mission.description: Cobaltpay rebuilt its REST API cobaltpay-rates last night (new Terraform module, new API id), and the Lambda function cobaltpay-fx-rates behind GET /rates is supposed to be invokable only by that API. The old API's resource-based permission on the function was left behind and nobody added one for the new API. On real AWS the new API would answer 500 ("Execution failed due to configuration error: Invalid permissions on Lambda function") and the security team also flags the leftover grant to an API that no longer exists. The emulator used in this environment does not enforce Lambda invoke permissions, so you have to inspect the function's resource policy yourself to see the problem.
mission.objective: Fix the resource-based policy of cobaltpay-fx-rates so that the principal apigateway.amazonaws.com may invoke it only on behalf of the current cobaltpay-rates API (and only for GET /rates, no wildcard over all APIs), and so that no statement referring to a different API remains. The API must keep answering GET /rates on stage live.

mission.name: Ready, Tested, Invisible
mission.description: Skyhook ships a weather API for drone pilots. The REST API skyhook-weather (GET /conditions, backed by the Lambda skyhook-conditions) was finished and tested on the stage dev last week. Release day came, the mobile app was published pointing at the stage prod, and every request returns 404 {"message":"Not Found"}. The API configuration itself is complete. The function reads a stage variable named tier from the request so that it can tell callers which environment answered, and ops wants production to say production.
mission.objective: Publish skyhook-weather on a stage named prod so that GET /conditions there works and reports the stage variable tier set to production. Leave dev as it is.

mission.name: The Browser Says No
mission.description: Zestlist is a to-do web app served from https://app.zestlist.example. It loads tasks with fetch("/tasks", {credentials: "include"}) from the REST API zestlist-api (stage web). curl works perfectly, but in the browser the console shows "blocked by CORS policy: Response to preflight request doesn't pass access control check". The GET /tasks method is wired to the Lambda zestlist-tasks with a non-proxy integration, so the function itself knows nothing about CORS and API Gateway has to supply the headers. The app sends an Authorization header and a JSON content type, and may later use POST.
mission.objective: Make /tasks on stage web browser-friendly for the origin https://app.zestlist.example: the preflight (OPTIONS) request must be answered with that exact origin, the methods GET and POST and the headers Content-Type and Authorization, and the real GET response must carry the same Access-Control-Allow-Origin header. A wildcard origin is not acceptable, because the app sends credentials.

mission.name: Zero Tolerance
mission.description: Ticketdash sells festival tickets through the REST API ticketdash-api (stage v2). During the Friday launch, 100% of requests failed with HTTP 429 Too Many Requests. A security hardening script had "locked down" the stage by setting its default throttling to rate 0 and burst 0, and nobody noticed that zero does not mean "unlimited". Besides browsing (GET /events), the API has the expensive route POST /checkout, which talks to a payment provider that tolerates at most about 20 requests per second. The emulator used here does not count requests, so you will have to inspect the stage settings rather than provoke a real 429.
mission.objective: Give stage v2 sane throttling: a default rate between 50 and 1000 requests per second with a burst between that rate and 2000, and a stricter override for POST /checkout of 1 to 20 requests per second (burst not above 40). Both routes must keep answering.

mission.name: Token in the Wrong Pocket
mission.description: Vaultline gives partner banks programmatic access to documents through GET /documents on the REST API vaultline-api (stage partner). The method is protected by a Lambda authorizer (vaultline-gatekeeper) that approves the partner token vl-partner-7731. Partners send that token in the header X-Vaultline-Token, as the integration guide says, and they all receive HTTP 401 Unauthorized. The authorizer function itself is fine, and so are the tokens. Someone tried to "fix" it earlier by switching the method to no authorization, then reverted when the security team noticed.
mission.objective: Make partner calls with the header X-Vaultline-Token: vl-partner-7731 succeed on GET /documents of vaultline-api stage partner, while calls without the header still get 401 and calls with a wrong token get 403. The method must remain protected by the existing authorizer.

mission.name: Lost in Translation
mission.description: Crateful's partner shops reserve stock with POST /reservations on the REST API crateful-api (stage live). The method uses a non-proxy Lambda integration: API Gateway reshapes the public JSON body with a mapping template before the function crateful-reserve sees it. Partners send {"productCode": "SKU-77", "quantity": 4, "note": "gift wrap"}. The function wants {"sku": ..., "qty": ..., "note": ...} (qty as a JSON number) and answers 400 "sku required" whenever the mapped value comes out empty, which is now every time. The template was written against an old version of the partner contract and nobody updated it. Notes are free text and may contain quotes.
mission.objective: Fix the request mapping template of POST /reservations so that productCode reaches the function as sku, quantity as the number qty, and note as text that survives quotes. The reservation for SKU-77 with 4 units must succeed.

mission.name: A Key to Nowhere
mission.description: Trailmix publishes hiking-trail data to partner apps through GET /trails on the REST API trailmix-api (stage v1). The method requires an API key. Account management issued two keys: trailmix-partner-key for the paying partner WanderPath and trailmix-trial-key for a prospect who has not signed yet. The partner reports "Forbidden" on every call even though they send their key in the x-api-key header. The contract with WanderPath is a usage plan of at most 20 requests per second (burst 40) and 10,000 requests per day. The prospect must stay locked out until the contract is signed.
mission.objective: Make GET /trails on trailmix-api stage v1 work for the partner key under a usage plan matching the contract (rate 20, burst 40, quota 10,000 per DAY), while requests without a key and requests with the trial key keep being refused.

mission.name: One Setting for the Whole Browser
mission.description: Mapleboard is a team planning tool at https://boards.maple.example. Its new backend is an HTTP API (API Gateway v2) called mapleboard-http, stage prod, with GET /boards and POST /boards served by the Lambda mapleboard-boards. The front end sends cookies (credentials: "include") and a JSON content type. The first deploy to staging worked in curl, but in the browser every request dies with a CORS error, even though the team has read that HTTP APIs can do CORS "with one setting". Nobody has made that setting yet, and a colleague's attempt with a wildcard origin was rejected in code review.
mission.objective: Configure CORS on the HTTP API mapleboard-http so that the preflight from the origin https://boards.maple.example is approved for GET and POST with the Content-Type header and credentials, actual responses carry the matching origin headers, and other origins are not approved.

mission.name: Yes Means Yes
mission.description: Pinecone Labs exposes an internal metrics feed through an HTTP API (API Gateway v2) named pinecone-metrics, stage prod, route GET /metrics. A Lambda authorizer, pinecone-bouncer, protects it: it looks at the header x-pine-key and answers with the short JSON form {"isAuthorized": true|false}, which is the format the team's new platform template uses. Since the authorizer was attached, every call, valid key or not, ends in HTTP 500 Internal Server Error, and the function logs show it returned exactly what it was supposed to. The authorizer function must not be changed.
mission.objective: Make GET /metrics on pinecone-metrics stage prod return the metrics for callers sending x-pine-key: pine-7a21, refuse callers with a wrong key (403) and callers with no key (401), without touching the authorizer function's code and without removing the authorizer from the route.
concepts: simple responses vs IAM policy responses

mission.name: Two Dialects of the Same Event
mission.description: Fernwood Freight quotes shipping prices through an HTTP API (API Gateway v2), fernwood-quotes, stage prod, route GET /quotes/{zone}. The Lambda fernwood-pricing was ported from a code sample for the "2.0" event format: it reads requestContext.http.method and rawPath, takes the zone from the path and the weight from the query string, and simply returns a dictionary, relying on API Gateway to wrap it into an HTTP response. The route was created through the console wizard of an older tutorial. Every request now ends with 500 Internal Server Error, while invoking the function directly with the sample event works perfectly. The function must not be modified.
mission.objective: Make GET /quotes/eu?weight=12 on fernwood-quotes stage prod return the quote from fernwood-pricing, with the zone, weight and HTTP method echoed correctly, by correcting the API-side configuration.

mission.name: Nobody Invited the Lambda
mission.description: Tidewater Freight prints a shipping label for every parcel through the state machine tidewater-label-flow, which calls the Lambda function print-shipping-label. The workflow was created last night by a teammate who copied the execution role from another project. Since then every execution dies on its very first step and the loading dock is hand-writing labels. The Lambda function itself has been tested and works.
mission.objective: Make tidewater-label-flow succeed for a parcel such as {"shipmentId": "TF-1042"}, by changing what the state machine's execution role is allowed to do. The role may call print-shipping-label and nothing else: the sibling function print-customs-form must stay off limits.

mission.name: Ghost Function
mission.description: Harborview Pharmacy approves prescription refills through the state machine harborview-refill-flow. Last sprint the platform team tidied up Lambda names and the function behind the eligibility check was renamed. The refill app now shows "Could not verify refill, please call the pharmacy" for every customer. The Lambda team insists their function is healthy and answers direct invocations. IAM has been reviewed and is not the issue.
mission.objective: Make harborview-refill-flow approve a refill for {"rx": "RX-5521", "dose": 2} using the production eligibility function (not the staging copy that happens to sit next to it).

mission.name: Fell Through the Cracks
mission.description: Brightwave Telecom triages support tickets with the state machine brightwave-ticket-triage. Urgent tickets page the on-call engineer, high priority ones go to the escalation queue and normal ones to the backlog, and that part works. But customers who file "low" tickets get an automated "something went wrong" email, and those tickets never reach anyone. The failed executions are piling up in the console.
mission.objective: Make brightwave-ticket-triage deliver every ticket to exactly one queue: urgent to bw-pager, high to bw-escalations, and every other priority (normal, low, or any value the app adds later) to bw-backlog.

mission.name: Where Did My Order Go
mission.description: Lumen Wholesale screens every new order with the state machine lumen-order-screening: a Lambda computes a fraud score, then the order is queued for the review desk. The reviewers complain that the messages in lumen-review-desk are "just a score" with no order number, customer or items, so they cannot tell what to review. The fraud-score Lambda is correct and the queue permissions are fine.
mission.objective: Make each message that lumen-order-screening puts on lumen-review-desk carry the complete original order (orderId, customer and items) together with the fraud score the Lambda computed.

mission.name: Literally Dollar
mission.description: Saffron Meal Kits stores every new subscriber in DynamoDB through the state machine saffron-signup. The marketing lead noticed two oddities in the saffron-subscribers table: the number of subscribers never grows past one row, and the "welcomeLine" column reads like source code instead of a greeting. All executions report SUCCEEDED, the role and the table are fine.
mission.objective: Make saffron-signup store one item per subscriber, keyed by the subscriber's real email address, with welcomeLine holding the finished sentence, for example "Welcome to Saffron, Noor Haddad! Your family plan starts with 3 boxes."

mission.name: Truthy Parcels
mission.description: Quillon Courier lets shippers pay extra for express delivery. The booking API puts "express": true on a parcel, and the state machine quillon-dispatch is supposed to drop those parcels on the express lane. Support is flooded: express customers say their parcels sit in the standard lane, and ops adds that older partner integrations, which do not send the field at all, have started to bring executions down. No executions fail for the new web app, they just go to the wrong lane.
mission.objective: Make quillon-dispatch send parcels with "express": true to quillon-express-lane, and every other parcel (express false, or no express field at all) to quillon-standard-lane, without any execution failing.

mission.name: Try, Try Again
mission.description: Fernhill Garden Centre reserves stock for each online order line through the state machine fernhill-reserve. The stock service is locked for a few seconds every time the warehouse scanner syncs, and during that window the Lambda fernhill-reserve-stock raises a StockLocked error. The workflow already has a Retry block copied from the AWS documentation, yet orders placed during a sync still fail outright instead of waiting for the lock to clear. Orders for SKUs that do not exist are rightly rejected and should keep failing immediately.
mission.objective: Make fernhill-reserve ride out a short stock lock: a reservation that hits StockLocked for a few seconds must end up SUCCEEDED. A request for an unknown SKU must still fail on the first attempt, with no retries wasted on it.

mission.name: Silent Failure
mission.description: Pinecrest Tickets charges cards through the state machine pinecrest-checkout and then sends a receipt. The finance team ran their monthly reconciliation and found 212 orders marked SUCCEEDED in Step Functions that were never paid for. Customers whose cards were declined got neither a receipt nor an explanation, and the dashboards show a spotless success rate. The charge Lambda is doing its job: it raises CardDeclined.
mission.objective: When the card is declined, pinecrest-checkout must tell the customer and fail honestly: put a message on pinecrest-declined that contains the orderId and the reason from the error, and end the execution as FAILED. Paid orders must keep succeeding, with a receipt on pinecrest-receipts and nothing on pinecrest-declined.

mission.name: A Week Is Not Always a Week
mission.description: Halcyon CRM sends a "your trial ends soon" reminder through the state machine halcyon-trial-reminder. The sign-up service starts one execution per trial and passes the exact moment the reminder is due as remindAt, an ISO 8601 timestamp such as 2026-03-14T09:30:00Z. Customers on 3-day and 14-day trials all received their reminders exactly one week after they signed up, which is wrong for everybody except the 7-day plan. Support also notices that some executions have been running for days.
mission.objective: Make halcyon-trial-reminder wait until the moment given in the execution's remindAt field and only then put the reminder message on halcyon-reminders. Triggers with different remindAt values must produce reminders at different times, and a reminder must never go out before its due time.

mission.name: Two Branches, One Array
mission.description: Orbit Mobile builds a customer "profile card" for its call-centre screen. The state machine orbit-profile-card looks up billing and data usage at the same time in a Parallel state, then publishes one compact message to the queue orbit-profile-cards with the customerId, plan and gbUsed. Since the two lookups were made parallel, every execution dies at the publish step with a path error, even though both Lambdas return the right data.
mission.objective: Make orbit-profile-card publish, for a customer such as C-5521, a message to orbit-profile-cards of the form {"customerId": ..., "plan": ..., "gbUsed": ...} with the real values from the two lookups. The two lookups must stay in parallel branches.

mission.name: One Bad Parcel
mission.description: Kestrel Logistics imports a nightly manifest with the state machine kestrel-manifest-import. A Map state validates each parcel and puts the accepted ones on kestrel-accepted, tagged with the manifest's batchId. After last week's release nothing is accepted at all, and before that release a single malformed parcel (a zero weight from a faulty scale) used to take the entire 4,000-parcel manifest down with it. Operations wants both problems solved properly: good parcels flow, and bad ones are set aside for a human instead of being lost.
mission.objective: Make kestrel-manifest-import succeed for a manifest such as {"batchId": "B-2041", "parcels": [...]} that contains one malformed parcel: every valid parcel is delivered to kestrel-accepted with its batchId, and the malformed one is sent to kestrel-quarantine together with its batchId, its id and the reason it was rejected. A malformed parcel must not appear on kestrel-accepted.

mission.name: The Approver Never Called Back
mission.description: Brightline Procurement holds every purchase order until a manager approves it. The state machine brightline-po-approval posts a request on the brightline-approvals queue and then waits for the manager's tool to call back. Managers say they get the request but approving does nothing, and the executions pile up in RUNNING until they time out three days later. The finance director also wants rejections handled: a rejected order must tell the requester why. Those executions currently end as FAILED and the requester hears nothing.
mission.objective: Make the approval round trip work end to end. When a manager approves a request with the callback they receive (aws stepfunctions send-task-success) the order must be published on brightline-issued with its poId. When a manager rejects it (send-task-failure with error "Rejected" and a cause), the requester must receive a message with the poId and the cause on brightline-requester-notices, the execution must end SUCCEEDED (a rejected order is a normal business outcome, not a system failure) and no order may be issued.

mission.name: Friday Release
mission.description: Marlin Bank's card-payment guard, the state machine marlin-limit-check, is called by the payments platform through its alias "live". Payments of EUR 1,000 or more must go to a human reviewer; smaller ones are approved automatically. Version 2 shipped this afternoon (it switched to the new currency-conversion Lambda) and the alias was moved to it. Since then the fraud desk sees no large payments at all: everything is auto-approved. The on-call engineer first thought of "just roll the alias back to version 1", but a colleague warns that version 1 stopped working when its old conversion function was retired weeks ago.
mission.objective: Make the alias marlin-limit-check:live decide correctly again: payments of EUR 1,000 or more (after conversion, boundary included) resolve to REVIEW, smaller ones to APPROVE, and every execution started through the alias succeeds. All the alias's traffic must go to one version that behaves correctly; no canary split between a good and a bad version.

mission.name: Four Dominoes
mission.description: Cedarpoint Retail's shop publishes an OrderPlaced event on the default event bus whenever a customer pays. An EventBridge rule, cedarpoint-order-placed, is meant to start the state machine cedarpoint-fulfilment, which allocates stock through a Lambda function and records the fulfilment in the DynamoDB table cedarpoint-fulfilments. Nothing has been recorded since the weekend's migration: the warehouse team prints orders by hand. Several people have "fixed one thing" each and nothing changed, because more than one link in the chain is broken, and every link hides the next one.
mission.objective: Make a real OrderPlaced event from source cedarpoint.shop (detail with orderId and items) end up as a fulfilment row in cedarpoint-fulfilments, by way of the event bus rule, the cedarpoint-fulfilment state machine and its Lambda. Events from other sources or of other types (such as OrderCancelled) must not start the workflow.
concepts: Step Functions as a rule target

mission.name: Door Without a Handle
mission.description: Brewline, a coffee-subscription startup, just shipped version 3 of its mobile app. The app signs customers in with the plain username-and-password call (InitiateAuth with USER_PASSWORD_AUTH) against the user pool brewline-customers, app client brewline-app. Every sign-in attempt, even by nora with the right password, now bounces with an error that has nothing to do with her password. The web dashboard, which uses secure remote password (SRP) sign-in on the same client, still works and must keep working.
mission.objective: Make customer nora (password Latte-Art-2024!) able to sign in through the brewline-app client with the username-and-password flow and receive tokens, keep token refresh and the existing SRP sign-in working on that client, and do not enable server-side admin flows on a client that ships inside a mobile app.

mission.name: Twenty-Four Characters of Pain
mission.description: Tidewater Books lets readers create an account in its app, which calls SignUp on the user pool tidewater-readers (client tidewater-web). Since the security review last week, nearly every new reader is turned away with InvalidPasswordException and the sign-up funnel has collapsed. Support tickets quote passwords such as "Tidewater42Books", which readers consider perfectly respectable. Product and security agreed on the rule: at least 10 characters with an upper-case letter, a lower-case letter and a digit. Symbols are not required.
mission.objective: Change the password policy of tidewater-readers so that a new reader can sign up with Tidewater42Books, while passwords that are shorter than 10 characters or lack an upper-case letter, a lower-case letter or a digit are still rejected.

mission.name: Welcome Aboard, Please Wait
mission.description: Lumen Logistics onboards dispatchers by creating them in the user pool lumen-dispatch with a temporary password. Ines started on Monday with the temporary password Temp-Welcome-0001! and has not changed it yet. Her portal (client lumen-portal) calls the plain username-and-password sign-in, and for her it never returns tokens: the response is a "challenge" that the portal does not know how to answer, so she sees a blank screen. Her colleague Tomas, who started last month, signs in without trouble. HR has told Ines to use the new password Harbor-Crane-81x from now on.
mission.objective: Make ines able to sign in to lumen-portal with the password Harbor-Crane-81x and receive tokens straight from the username-and-password call, without recreating her account or touching Tomas.

mission.name: Check Your Inbox
mission.description: Kestrel Fitness lets members register in its app against the user pool kestrel-members. Kai signed up yesterday with the password Sprint-Interval-9! and has been trying to sign in ever since, getting "User is not confirmed". Cognito emailed a six-digit verification code to kai@example.com, but Kai says it never arrived. In this lab all outgoing mail is captured by the emulator and can be read at the emulator's endpoint URL followed by /_aws/ses. The product owner also wants the member's email to end up verified, because password resets are sent to it.
mission.objective: Make kai able to sign in to the app client kestrel-ios with the password chosen at sign-up, with the email address marked as verified so that the "forgot password" flow works for Kai as well.

mission.name: Never Ship a Secret
mission.description: Quill, a note-taking app, keeps accounts in the user pool quill-accounts. Its backend signs users in through the app client quill-web, which has a client secret and works fine. For the new mobile app the developers copied that client's ID into the code, and since the release every sign-in from a phone fails with an error about a missing SECRET_HASH. Embedding the secret in an app that anyone can download and unpack was rejected by the security team in review. User mira (password Margin-Notes-55!) is the test account.
mission.objective: Give the mobile app its own app client named quill-mobile, one that it can use with just a username and password (no client secret) and that also supports refreshing sessions. Mira must be able to sign in and refresh through it. The backend's quill-web client must keep working unchanged, with its secret.

mission.name: Reset Goes Nowhere
mission.description: Pinecrest Library's patrons manage their cards in a portal backed by the user pool pinecrest-patrons (client pinecrest-portal). Omar, a patron since the desk staff imported the old card database last week, clicked "Forgot password" and got an error instead of an email. Lena, who registered herself, can reset hers without trouble. The library's records say Omar's email address is omar@example.com. In this lab, outgoing mail is captured by the emulator and can be read at the emulator's endpoint URL followed by /_aws/ses.
mission.objective: Make the self-service password reset work for omar: starting "forgot password" for him must deliver a code to omar@example.com, and completing the reset with that code must let him sign in with the new password. Lena's account must stay as it is.

mission.name: Admin in Name Only
mission.description: Parcelpost's internal console decides who may open the "Reroute shipments" screen by looking at the cognito:groups claim of the ID token: the group ops-admins is allowed, everyone else is read-only. Dara, the operations lead, signs in through the app client parcelpost-console of the user pool parcelpost-staff, and still gets the read-only view. Eli from support correctly sees the read-only view. Both passwords are Parcel-Route-2024! and Dara swears she was added to the admin group months ago.
mission.objective: Make a fresh sign-in by dara return an ID token whose cognito:groups claim contains ops-admins, while eli's tokens must not contain it and must still show his support group.

mission.name: One Flag Too Few
mission.description: Skylark Air's booking SPA uses the app client skylark-spa in the user pool skylark-travelers. Its contract with the app team: username-and-password sign-in, refreshable sessions, access and ID tokens valid for 30 minutes, refresh tokens valid for 14 days. Yesterday a developer added a second callback URL (https://preview.example.com/cb) for preview deployments with a single update-user-pool-client call that listed the callback URLs and the OAuth settings the CLI complained about. Since then the app cannot sign anybody in, and nobody changed the user pool or the users (test account: yuki, password Window-Seat-12A!). The hosted-UI login for the two callback URLs must keep working.
mission.objective: Restore the skylark-spa client to its contract (password sign-in and refresh working, access and ID tokens valid for exactly 30 minutes, refresh token valid for 14 days) without losing the preview callback URL or the hosted-UI authorization-code login on both callback URLs.

mission.name: Provisioner Denied
mission.description: Fernwood's HR system onboards every new hire automatically. It runs as the IAM user fernwood-provisioner and is supposed to create the person in the user pool fernwood-staff, set their first permanent password, and add them to the group employees.
