After last month's migration, which rebuilt the pool, the onboarding job fails with AccessDeniedException on the Cognito calls. The job also looks accounts up with admin-get-user. Fernwood has a second pool, fernwood-contractors, that this job has never been allowed to touch, and nobody wants this job to be able to delete people.
mission.objective: Make fernwood-provisioner able to create users in fernwood-staff, read them back, set their password and add them to a group, using a least-privilege policy: no access to fernwood-contractors, and no permission to delete users.
concepts: IAM permissions for Cognito admin APIs

mission.name: Read-Only Robot
mission.description: Stockroom's nightly sync job pushes warehouse counts to the inventory API. It authenticates with the OAuth client-credentials grant against the token endpoint of the user pool stockroom-machines, as the app client nightly-sync, and asks for the scopes inventory/read and inventory/write. Since the API was split off, the token endpoint answers with invalid_scope and the counts have not been updated for three days. The dashboard client stockroom-dashboard in the same pool is read-only by design. The pool has a resource server with the identifier inventory.
mission.objective: Make the client-credentials grant for nightly-sync succeed with both inventory/read and inventory/write in the resulting access token. The inventory/admin scope must stay defined but out of reach for nightly-sync, and the dashboard client must still be unable to obtain inventory/write.

mission.name: Lost in Redirect
mission.description: Marigold sells tickets to local events. Its single-page app sends visitors to the Cognito hosted login of the user pool marigold-fans (app client marigold-web) using the authorization-code flow, with the callback URL https://marigold.example.com/auth/callback. Since the app moved to production, the hosted login never even shows a form: the authorize request is rejected. The developer who set the client up months ago also left http://localhost:3000/callback registered, which the front-end team still uses on their laptops. Fan noor (password Front-Row-Seats-3!) is the test account.
mission.objective: Make the complete hosted-UI login work for the production callback URL (authorize, sign in as noor, receive a code, exchange it for tokens), keep the localhost callback working, accept no other callback URL, and do not leave the deprecated implicit flow enabled on the client.

mission.name: The Bouncer Who Forgot to Answer
mission.description: Brightpath Staffing lets partner agencies register themselves in the user pool brightpath-partners (client brightpath-portal). A pre sign-up Lambda function, brightpath-presignup, is meant to confirm accounts instantly when the email address is from a partner domain (partner.example.com or agency.example.org) and leave everyone else on the normal email-code flow. After its last edit, partner staff get a cryptic "invalid Lambda response" error during registration, and people typing their company address with capital letters (Dev@Partner.Example.com) report the same trouble on top of it. Public sign-ups from other domains are behaving correctly. The function's source is in presignup.py in your workspace.
mission.objective: Make partner sign-ups succeed and be confirmed on the spot, with the email marked as verified, whatever the capitalisation of the address, so that the new account can sign in right away. Sign-ups from any other domain must still succeed but stay unconfirmed.

mission.name: Claims Vanish
mission.description: Cobalt's multi-tenant SaaS keeps customer data apart with a tenant claim: a pre token generation Lambda (cobalt-claims) copies each user's custom:tenant attribute into the ID token of the user pool cobalt-tenants (client cobalt-app), and every API trusts that claim. Ava belongs to tenant acme, Ben to globex (both use the password Tenant-Wall-2024!). Yesterday the platform team wired a welcome-email function (cobalt-welcome) to the pool as a post confirmation trigger, and released a small refactor of cobalt-claims. Since then the APIs return empty data for everybody: tokens no longer contain a tenant claim. The welcome email must keep working. The sources of both functions are in your workspace (claims.py, welcome.py).
mission.objective: Make a fresh sign-in by ava produce an ID token with the claim tenant set to acme, and by ben one with tenant set to globex, while keeping the cobalt-welcome post confirmation trigger attached to the pool.
concepts: Lambda config is replaced as a whole

mission.name: Stolen Session
mission.description: Halyard, a maritime logistics company, got an alert at 03:12: crew member mara was signed in from two continents at once. Her password, Anchor-Chain-0451!, turned up in a credential dump and an attacker has been using her account through the app client halyard-app of the user pool halyard-crew. Security already captured two of the attacker's sessions (access and refresh tokens) in the bucket halyard-ir-evidence, but the logs are patchy and the attacker may have signed in other times as well. Another crew member, noah, is mid-shift on a vessel with a valid session and must not be disrupted. Mara is asleep and must be able to get back into her account later.
mission.objective: Cut the attacker off: none of the captured sessions, nor any other session that was opened with Mara's leaked password, may still work (neither the access token nor the refresh token), and the leaked password itself must stop working. Mara's account must not be deleted or left disabled (she has to be able to recover it), and noah's session and sign-in must be untouched.

mission.name: Ghost Town Storefront
mission.description: Pageturn Books put their storefront behind an Application Load Balancer last night. The web server is up (an instance named pageturn-web-1), the load balancer is active and has a listener on port 80, yet every visitor gets an HTTP 503 error page. Nothing is wrong with the app itself; the load balancer just has nowhere to send the traffic.
mission.objective: Make http://pageturn-alb on port 80 serve the storefront from the pageturn-web-1 instance, and make sure the target group reports that instance as healthy.

mission.name: Right Address, Wrong Extension
mission.description: Tidewater Logistics exposes its parcel-tracking API through the load balancer tidewater-alb. After last night's deploy the tracking page shows errors and the target group tracking-api lists its only instance as unhealthy. The service itself is running fine on the instance (the team can see it answering on its usual port), and the target group's own port setting was not touched.
mission.objective: Get the tracking API answering through tidewater-alb on port 80, with every target registered in the group tracking-api reporting healthy.

mission.name: Taking the Pulse
mission.description: Brewline Coffee runs its mobile-ordering API on two instances behind the load balancer brewline-alb. Ops dashboards have been red since the Terraform apply an hour ago: both targets in the group brewline-orders show "unhealthy", even though customers can still place orders (an ALB with no healthy targets keeps sending traffic anyway, which is exactly why nobody noticed sooner). The API team swears the service is up and says it exposes a dedicated liveness endpoint; the root URL is not a page, it is just a 404.
mission.objective: Make both targets of brewline-orders healthy by fixing the group's health check so it asks a question the API actually answers with success. Do not make the check accept error responses just to turn the dashboard green.

mission.name: Members Meet the Staging Build
mission.description: Maplewood Credit Union's online-banking portal sits behind the load balancer maplewood-alb. This morning members started seeing a grey "STAGING BUILD" banner and half-finished screens. Both the production and the staging fleet are up and healthy, each in its own target group (portal-prod and portal-staging). During last night's release rehearsal someone changed how the load balancer decides where traffic goes.
mission.objective: Members visiting maplewood-alb on port 80 must get the production portal again. The staging target group and its instance must stay in place for testers.

mission.name: Admin Door Left Ajar
mission.description: Corallo Cart's load balancer corallo-alb splits traffic by path: the shop front end serves everything, and /api/* goes to the API fleet. A penetration tester just reported that anyone on the internet can open /api/admin/users. The team is sure they added a listener rule that blocks /api/admin/* with a 403 last month, and the rule is still in the listener. It simply never seems to fire.
mission.objective: Requests for /api/admin/* through corallo-alb on port 80 must be answered with HTTP 403 by the load balancer itself. Other /api/* paths must still reach the API fleet, and everything else must still reach the shop front end.

mission.name: One Letter Off
mission.description: HelixPay serves several hostnames from one load balancer, helix-alb, and picks the fleet by the Host header: the customer app lives on portal.helixpay.example and app.helixpay.example, while everything else lands on the marketing site. After a DNS cleanup, support tickets say "portal works but app. shows the marketing page". Both hostnames resolve to the load balancer correctly, and both are meant to be served by the same fleet.
mission.objective: Make both portal.helixpay.example and app.helixpay.example reach the customer portal fleet through helix-alb, while any other host still lands on the marketing fleet.

mission.name: Secure by Redirect
mission.description: Quillstone Publishing wants every visitor on plain HTTP to be bounced to HTTPS by the load balancer quillstone-alb itself (the TLS listener on 443 is the platform team's job and already exists elsewhere). The security review of the existing port-80 redirect found three problems: browsers and search engines do not remember it as the permanent move it should be, people clicking a link to a deep page such as /pricing?plan=pro end up on the home page, and the redirect points at a non-standard TLS port that firewalls often block.
mission.objective: Make the port-80 listener of quillstone-alb answer every request with a permanent redirect to the same host on the standard HTTPS port 443, keeping the original path and query string.

mission.name: Cart Amnesia
mission.description: Kestrel Outfitters keeps each shopper's cart in the memory of whichever web server handled the first request (a decision for the next quarter's backlog). Since the second web server joined target group kestrel-web behind kestrel-alb, customers report that items "vanish" from their cart every other click: their requests bounce between the two servers, and only one of them knows about the cart. A rewrite to a shared session store is planned, but not this week.
mission.objective: Make kestrel-alb keep each shopper on the same server for at least a day, using a cookie generated by the load balancer, while still spreading new shoppers across both servers.

mission.name: The Night Shift Never Ended
mission.description: Lumenbeam's video-thumbnail API runs in the Auto Scaling group lumen-api-asg behind lumen-alb. Last week finance asked for a cost-saving "night mode"; an engineer scaled the group down by hand and added a scheduled action called nightly-shutdown. Now it is Monday morning, every request gets a 503, and the group has no instances at all. Whoever fixes it should not have to repeat the fix tonight.
mission.objective: Bring lumen-api-asg back so lumen-alb serves traffic from at least two healthy instances, with room to grow to at least six when load spikes, and make sure no scheduled action will switch the service off again.

mission.name: Orphaned Fleet
mission.description: Orbit Rides' dispatch API moved to an Auto Scaling group, orbit-dispatch-asg, behind the load balancer orbit-alb. The migration ticket is closed, the group shows two InService instances, the instances answer when called directly, and yet orbit-alb returns 503 to every rider app. An engineer's quick workaround last week was to register the instance IDs by hand; the on-call knows that would break the next time an instance is replaced.
mission.objective: Wire the Auto Scaling group to the target group orbit-dispatch so that orbit-alb serves traffic, and so that replacement instances join the target group on their own without anyone running register-targets.

mission.name: Version One Forever
mission.description: Parcelway Courier's routing service runs in the Auto Scaling group parcelway-asg behind parcelway-alb. Release 2.3 shipped with a bad startup script: the service came up on the wrong port, and the group's two instances have been failing health checks since. The developers fixed the script yesterday and published it as a new version of the launch template parcelway-lt. Instances keep launching with the old behaviour anyway, and terminating them by hand just produces the same broken instances again.
mission.objective: Get parcelway-alb serving release 2.4 from healthy instances. Every instance in the group must be running the corrected launch template version, and the group itself must be set up so future instances use it too.

mission.name: Out of Breath
mission.description: Fathomly's analytics dashboard API runs on two instances in the target group fathomly-api behind fathomly-alb. Since the team added a "deep" dependency probe to the /health endpoint, both targets bounce to unhealthy with the reason Target.Timeout. The endpoint is not broken: asked directly it answers with HTTP 200 and { "db": "ok" }, it just takes a while because it checks the reporting database. The app also has a trivial /livez route that answers instantly.
mission.objective: Make both targets of fathomly-api healthy again with a health check that is sane: it must fail fast enough to detect a real outage within about two minutes, and its timing settings must be valid for the load balancer.

mission.name: Cutover Night
mission.description: Saffron Street's checkout service is mid blue/green migration. The blue fleet (release 1, two instances in the group saffron-blue-asg) serves everyone; the green fleet (release 2, group saffron-green-asg) has been deployed but still receives no traffic because the weighted forward action on saffron-alb sends 100 percent to blue. Tonight is the cutover. The runbook says: all traffic to green, blue stays registered with weight 0 for one hour as an instant rollback, and never shift traffic to a fleet smaller than the one it replaces. The green group currently runs a single instance.
mission.objective: Complete the cutover on saffron-alb: every request is answered by release 2, the green fleet has at least as many healthy instances as blue, and blue remains attached to the listener with weight 0 (with its instances still healthy) so rollback is one command away.

mission.name: Internal Affairs
mission.description: Nimbus Notes launched its public API gateway this morning, and nobody outside the VPC can reach it. The gateway is the load balancer nimbus-gateway, whose scheme turns out to be "internal". It routes by hostname and path (the API hostname goes to the API fleet, /status answers by itself, everything else is the web fleet) and the routing is exactly what the product team wants. Only the exposure is wrong, and the scheme of a load balancer cannot be edited.
mission.objective: Replace nimbus-gateway with an internet-facing Application Load Balancer that spans at least two Availability Zones and reproduces the same routing on the same listener port, using the existing target groups. The internal load balancer must be gone when you are done so there is only one gateway to maintain.

mission.name: Wrong Stream, Right Thermostat
mission.description: Thermowave sells smart thermostats. Every thermostat posts its temperature to an ingest function, thermo-ingest, which forwards each reading into the Kinesis stream that feeds the energy-saving model. Since Monday's release the model has seen no new data, and the function's error count in the dashboard is climbing. Nobody touched the stream and the function's IAM role is unchanged; the release only touched the function's configuration.
mission.objective: Make thermo-ingest deliver readings into the existing Thermowave stream again. Do not create extra streams, and keep every other setting of the function (firmware channel included) as it was.

mission.name: Scan and Deliver Denied
mission.description: Parcelhop's depot scanners send each batch of parcel scans through a gateway that signs in as the IAM user scan-gateway and calls PutRecords on the Kinesis stream parcel-scans. This morning the new Hamburg depot went live and every single batch comes back AccessDenied. The inline policy was copied from the staging environment by a colleague who has since gone on holiday. A second stream, parcel-billing, carries invoices and must stay off-limits to the scanners; scanners also have no business reading the stream back.
mission.objective: Let the user scan-gateway write batches of scans to the stream parcel-scans, and nothing more: no access to parcel-billing and no read access to parcel-scans.

mission.name: Short Memory
mission.description: Tidewater Energy streams smart-meter reads into the Kinesis stream meter-reads, where the billing system consumes them. Billing is being migrated to a new platform next weekend and will be offline for up to three days, during which reads keep arriving. The platform team must be able to replay everything from the start of the outage once billing is back, with a day of safety margin. Right now the stream only remembers its default window, and finance has noted that data kept beyond a week is billed as long-term retention they do not want to pay for.
mission.objective: Make meter-reads keep its data long enough to survive a three-day billing outage with a day to spare, but no longer than seven days. Do not recreate the stream: the reads already in it must stay.

mission.name: The Auditor Sees Nothing
mission.description: Sablecart's fraud team runs a nightly Lambda, swipe-audit, that walks the card-swipes stream and totals what it finds. Today six card swipes are sitting in the stream (you can see them yourself), yet the audit reports "0 swipes audited" and the totals are zero. The function runs without any error, its IAM role is fine, and the stream has plenty of retention left. Whoever wrote the reader says it "reads the shard from the top".
mission.objective: Make swipe-audit report every swipe that is currently retained in card-swipes, including swipes that arrive between now and the next run.

mission.name: One Key to Rule Them All
mission.description: Quillbox, an online stationery shop, publishes order events (created, paid, shipped) into the four-shard stream order-events through a Lambda called order-publisher. Its dashboard shows one shard pinned at its write limit while the other three are almost idle, and the warehouse consumer, which has to see each order's events in the order they happened, lags more every week. The stream was sized correctly: four shards are plenty for Quillbox's traffic. The problem is in how the publisher hands records to Kinesis.
mission.objective: Make order-publisher spread its events across the shards of order-events while every event of the same order still lands on the same shard, so the warehouse keeps seeing each order's events in order.

mission.name: Ceiling at One Megabyte
mission.description: Voltus runs a network of EV chargers. Every charger sends a heartbeat every few seconds into the one-shard stream charger-heartbeats. The roll-out of 2,000 new chargers next month will push the peak to about 3 MB per second, and the capacity planning review states a shard accepts 1 MB/s of writes. Heartbeats already in the stream must not be lost, and the finance team will not sign off on more than six shards.
mission.objective: Give charger-heartbeats enough write capacity for a 3 MB/s peak (at 1 MB/s per shard) with no more than six shards, keeping the existing stream and every record already in it. Heartbeats from different chargers must be accepted across the stream's shards.

mission.name: Sharing the Pipe
mission.description: Rivermill Exchange publishes every executed trade to the Kinesis stream trade-ticks. Two Lambdas consume it through event source mappings: ledger-writer books each trade in the ledger, and risk-scorer scores it for the risk desk. A third consumer, an old reporting app, also reads the stream. All of them split the same 2 MB/s of read capacity per shard, and during the opening auction the risk desk's scores fall minutes behind the market. The ledger is fine as it is. Only the risk-scorer needs to stop competing with the others.
mission.objective: Make risk-scorer read trade-ticks with read throughput that is dedicated to it instead of shared with the other consumers. Every trade must still be scored exactly once, and ledger-writer must keep working as it does today.

mission.name: Billed Twice at the Seam
mission.description: Brightline, a mobile operator, bills usage events from the Kinesis stream usage-events. A Lambda, billing-resume, runs every few minutes: it reads the checkpoint it stored in the SSM parameter /brightline/billing/checkpoint (the sequence number of the last event it billed), continues from there, writes one invoice line per event into the DynamoDB table invoice-lines, and saves the new checkpoint. Customer support keeps receiving the same complaint: the last usage event of the previous run shows up on the invoice twice. The function never fails and never skips an event.
mission.objective: Make billing-resume continue exactly where the previous run stopped: the event named by the checkpoint must not be billed again, every later event must be billed once, and the checkpoint must advance to the last event billed.

mission.name: Poison Pill in the Pipe
mission.description: Marlow Health streams patient-monitor readings into the Kinesis stream vitals. The Lambda vitals-alerter consumes it through an event source mapping and records every valid reading in the table vitals-processed. This morning one monitor with a firmware bug published a reading that is not valid JSON. Since then the alerts for that shard have been frozen: the function fails on the broken reading, is invoked with the same batch again and again, and the readings stored behind it are never processed. Clinical engineering wants the broken reading kept for analysis, but not in the way of everyone else.
mission.objective: Make the vitals-alerter mapping survive a malformed reading: valid readings in the same batch as a bad one, and those that arrive after it, must be processed, and the broken reading itself must be kept in the SQS queue vitals-dead-letters for later analysis.

mission.name: Clicks in the Wrong Lake
mission.description: Harborview Analytics collects web click events through the Amazon Data Firehose delivery stream clickstream-to-lake. The data engineers' Athena table reads s3://harborview-datalake/clicks/ and expects one folder per day named dt=YYYY-MM-DD (for example clicks/dt=2026-03-14/). Since the delivery stream was rebuilt last week, the table has stayed empty. Producers report no errors, Firehose reports no failures, and the delivery stream's role is fine. Someone has already noticed a bucket nobody recognises in the account.
mission.objective: Make clickstream-to-lake deliver new click events into the data lake bucket harborview-datalake, under clicks/ in a dt=YYYY-MM-DD folder for the day the event was received (UTC).

mission.name: Fifteen Minutes Too Late
mission.description: Aldermoor Bank's payment gateways send fraud signals to the Firehose delivery stream fraud-signals-to-s3, which lands them in s3://aldermoor-fraud-landing under signals/, where the fraud-analysis jobs pick them up. The analysts complain that signals arrive in the bucket about a quarter of an hour after the payment, far too late to stop a card. The storage team adds a second complaint: the landing bucket is growing quickly because the files are stored as plain text. Prefix, bucket and role are all correct; the delivery stream has simply never been tuned.
mission.objective: Make a fraud signal show up in aldermoor-fraud-landing under signals/ within about 30 seconds of being sent, stored gzip-compressed. Do not make Firehose write a new object more often than every few seconds: the analysis jobs struggle with swarms of tiny files.

mission.name: The Archive That Never Fills
mission.description: Pinecrest Media's apps publish page-view events into the Kinesis stream pageviews, where two real-time dashboards read them. Compliance also requires every event to be archived to S3, so a Firehose delivery stream, pageview-archive, was created to copy the stream into s3://pinecrest-archive under raw/. Months later an auditor opens the bucket: it is empty. The delivery stream is ACTIVE, shows no errors, and its role can write to the bucket. The apps must not be changed, and the real-time dashboards must keep reading pageviews exactly as they do today.
mission.objective: Make every event published to the Kinesis stream pageviews end up in the archive bucket under raw/ through the delivery stream named pageview-archive, without changing the pageviews stream or the way apps publish to it.

mission.name: Breaking the Transform Contract
mission.description: SwiftCab streams ride events into the data lake through the Firehose delivery stream ride-events-to-lake. A Lambda, ride-event-shaper, is attached to it as a transformation: it turns each raw ride event (cents, rider phone number and all) into a clean analytics line with the fare in dollars and without personal data. Since the function was rewritten last week the lake receives nothing useful: everything lands in the error folder ride-rejects/, including perfectly healthy events. Firehose and the bucket work, and the function runs without crashing on good input. A ride event that lacks a fare must not be loaded, but it should not take other events down with it either; those go to ride-rejects/ for the data team to inspect.
mission.objective: Make ride-event-shaper honour Firehose's transformation contract so valid ride events reach the lake under rides/ as one JSON document per line (ride_id, fare_usd, currency and pickup, no rider phone), while an event without a fare is rejected on its own into ride-rejects/ and other events in the same batch are unaffected.

mission.name: Orphaned Parents, Missing Children
mission.description: Ledgerline, a payments processor, writes account entries (account, a running seq number per account, amount) into the Kinesis stream ledger-entries. A Lambda, ledger-export, produces the nightly export for the reconciliation team: all entries still in the stream, grouped per account in the order they were written. The stream started with one shard and was resharded twice as traffic grew. The reconciliation team now reports that the export is missing every entry written since the first reshard and that new entries never show up at all. The function raises no error, and the stream, the retention and the data are fine.
mission.objective: Make ledger-export return every entry still retained in ledger-entries, including entries written after any reshard, each exactly once, and with each account's entries in the order they were written.

mission.name: The Blocked Pipeline
mission.description: Harbor & Vine Logistics indexes every overnight freight manifest with a Lambda function, hv-manifest-indexer. Since this morning the dispatch dashboard is empty and the function is failing. The incident ticket (INC-2291, in your workspace) says someone "froze" the old indexer at 03:40 and the 05:30 deploy touched the function. Nobody remembers exactly what changed, and more than one thing is wrong.
mission.objective: Get hv-manifest-indexer processing manifests again: it must read from s3://hv-manifests/incoming/, write to processed/, and record the result in the hv-manifest-index table. Do not widen the role beyond the manifests bucket, do not give it any access to hv-payroll-exports, and keep the contractor restriction on restricted/ intact.

mission.name: The Silent Chain
mission.description: Tidewater Tickets sells concert seats through a four-stage chain: the checkout service publishes to SNS, a queue buffers the events, a Lambda function fulfils them and writes the result to DynamoDB. After Tuesday's release nothing has been written to the fulfilment table, yet checkout reports every publish as successful. Support ticket TT-5530 is in your workspace. Each stage was touched by a different person.
mission.objective: Make a TicketSold event published to tt-ticket-events end up as an item in tt-fulfilled-tickets, while TicketRefunded events keep being kept out of the fulfilment queue. Do not rebuild the pipeline from scratch and do not remove the subscription's filtering.

mission.name: The Blind System
mission.description: Kestrel Payments lost four hours of settlement capacity on Saturday night and the on-call engineer was never paged. The monitoring chain looks complete on paper: log group, metric filter, alarm, SNS topic, pager queue. Yet when the API logs errors, nothing happens. The draft postmortem (in your workspace) describes what the monitoring was supposed to do.
mission.objective: Make a burst of ERROR lines in /kp/settlement-api put kp-settlement-errors into ALARM and deliver a notification to the pager queue, while ordinary INFO lines still produce no metric data.

mission.name: Upload Goes Nowhere
mission.description: Marigold Photo Studio's wedding photographers upload shoots to an S3 bucket and a Lambda function turns every JPEG into a gallery thumbnail. Since Monday's storage reorganisation the uploads succeed but no thumbnail ever appears. The escalation note is in your workspace; it mentions that the trigger and the IAM policy were both "copied from staging".
mission.objective: Uploading a .jpg to mg-photo-uploads must produce thumb-<name> in mg-photo-thumbs, uploading other file types must not, and uploads to the staging bucket must not trigger the production function. The thumbnailer may read from the uploads bucket but must never be able to write to it.

mission.name: The Dead API
mission.description: Quillmark Press migrated its partner catalogue API to a new API Gateway REST API on Friday afternoon. Since then every retail partner sees a different error: one gets 403, one gets "Stage not found", the mobile app times out. The incident ticket (INC-4417, in your workspace) lists the partner contract and what the migration team remembers doing.
mission.objective: A partner calling GET /prod/books with the partner API key must receive the catalogue from the qm-catalog-api function with HTTP 200. Calls without an API key must still be rejected, and the fix may not move the API onto a different stage name.

mission.name: Container Chaos
mission.description: Ledger & Co.'s month-end close page is served by an ECS Fargate service, ledger-web, which an engineer scaled down during a rollback drill. Now the finance team needs it and nobody can get a task to stay up. The service has no running tasks, and the task definition has not been touched since the drill. The incident ticket (INC-6120) is in your workspace.
mission.objective: Bring ledger-web in cluster ledger-prod back to two healthy running tasks that stay up, using a fixed task definition revision. Keep the container named "web" and keep the DB_HOST wrapper requirement; do not bypass it.

mission.name: Stream Silence
mission.description: Orbit Fitness' weekly step-challenge leaderboard stopped moving on Tuesday night. Workouts are still logged, but the Lambda function that converts each new workout into a leaderboard score never seems to run, or never succeeds. The change log in your workspace (ORBIT-1893) shows four people touching the pipeline within an hour.
mission.objective: Logging a workout in orbit-workouts must add its points to that user's score in orbit-leaderboard via the DynamoDB stream and the orbit-leaderboard-updater function. Keep both tables and their existing data, and keep the role limited to the leaderboard table.

mission.name: Stack Refuses to Update
mission.description: Cobalt Retail moved its order ledger into a CloudFormation stack, but the stack ended up in a failed state and the deploy bot won't touch it. Meanwhile finance has already started writing real entries into the table the stack created. Everyone's first suggestion is "delete it and start over". Change ticket CHG-2207, in your workspace, explains what the stack was meant to do and which neighbouring stack must not be disturbed.
mission.objective: Bring the cobalt-orders stack to a healthy *_COMPLETE state with its ledger function working, without losing the entries already in the cobalt-ledger table and without touching the legacy cobalt-core stack or its export. The stack must also be safe to delete in future without destroying the ledger.

mission.name: The Credential Crisis
mission.description: Juniper Health's claims portal has been returning 500s since 02:40 UTC, right after a failed credential rotation. To get past the failed rotation, an engineer deleted and re-created the database secret and loaded the new password into it. The database is healthy and already uses the new password, but nobody touched the application side. The SEV-1 ticket INC-9004 is in your workspace.
mission.objective: juniper-claims-api must authenticate again: its role has to be able to read the re-created juniper/prod/db-credentials secret, the function has to look the secret up correctly, and the secret's current version has to hold the password the database accepts. The role may read only this one secret.
concepts: Secrets Manager ARNs and version stages

mission.name: The Missing Bridge
mission.description: Ashgrove Audit has been engaged to audit Ferro Mining's Q3 ledger. Ferro's cloud team built a two-hop access path (auditor user, bridge role, ledger reader role) with an ExternalId on the first hop. On day one of fieldwork the auditor cannot get past the first step. The engagement note (FM-2026-Q3, in your workspace) gives the agreed design and the CISO's constraints.
mission.objective: The user ashgrove-auditor must be able to assume ferro-audit-bridge with the agreed ExternalId, chain into ferro-ledger-reader, and read s3://ferro-ledger-archive/2026/q3.csv. Assuming the bridge without the ExternalId must still fail, and the auditor must not be able to reach ferro-breakglass-admin.

mission.name: Security Audit
mission.description: An external red team turned Quasar Fintech's CI deploy role into full account administrator in a few minutes, using nothing but the permissions it already held (finding PT-2026-014, in your workspace). The report lists several independent escalation paths. The pipeline still has to ship tonight's release, so the role cannot simply be emptied.
mission.objective: Close every privilege-escalation path from qf-ci-deployer while keeping its legitimate duties working: deploying code to qf-* Lambda functions, creating functions with the standard qf-svc-lambda-exec role, and uploading to qf-build-artifacts. The role must not be able to mint admin roles, pass privileged roles, create credentials for other identities, or rewrite its own permissions.

mission.name: Data Exposure Incident
mission.description: A bug-bounty researcher downloaded a file full of customer PII from Ardent Analytics' export bucket without credentials, and mentioned that other access is too generous as well. The inventory of buckets and identities, and the history of the "temporary" changes that caused it, is in the incident file (SEC-INC-0719) in your workspace. Ardent's business must keep running while the exposure is closed.
mission.objective: Close every unintended read path to ardent-customer-exports (anyone with an unrelated identity, the temp contractor via the staff group, and one partner reading another partner's feed) while keeping the analyst's PII access, each partner's own feed, staff access to reports/, and the intentionally public logo in ardent-marketing-assets working.
concepts: S3 bucket policies and public principals

mission.name: Queue Meltdown
mission.description: A malformed parcel record entered Parcelwise's sort-jobs queue on Thursday and the sorter workers choked on it, again and again, for hours. Nobody was paged, and the poison message never left the queue. The ops review notes (in your workspace) describe the intended design (a dead-letter queue and a page) and the agreed numbers.
mission.objective: A message that keeps failing must be parked in pw-sort-jobs-dlq after a handful of receives (at most 5), the source queue must give a worker 30 seconds per parcel before handing the message to somebody else, and ops must get paged through pw-ops-alerts when the DLQ holds a message. Do not delete the queues.
concepts: SQS dead-letter queues and redrive policy

mission.name: Flying Blind
mission.description: Tallow & Finch's checkout Lambda failed one order in three for 47 minutes and nothing paged. The postmortem (PM-2026-31, in your workspace) lists the observability design that was supposed to catch this: structured JSON logs, a metric filter, an alarm and an SNS page. Every piece exists, but the monitoring chain carries nothing from the function's logs to the on-call queue.
mission.objective: A burst of failing checkouts (invoking tf-checkout-fn with {"fail": true}) must put the tf-checkout-errors alarm into ALARM and deliver a notification to the on-call pager queue (tf-oncall-inbox) through the production topic tf-oncall. Successful checkouts must not count as failures. Do not point production paging at the sandbox topic.

mission.name: The Unreachable Service
mission.description: Meridian Transit moved its mt-gateway ECS service into a new VPC as part of a "private subnets only" security programme. ECS reports the service running, but the load balancer health checks fail and the tasks cannot reach the internet for image pulls. The network design signed off by security, and the shortcuts taken during the migration, are in the incident file (INC-5561) in your workspace. The lab has no packet flow, so the fix is judged by task placement and by the route and security-group rules.
mission.objective: Make mt-gateway run only in the private subnet without public IPs, give that subnet an outbound route through the NAT gateway (not the internet gateway), allow HTTPS egress from the service's security group, and allow port 8080 inbound from the load balancer's security group only, never from the internet.

mission.name: Encryption Lockout
mission.description: At 07:40 Vaultline Clinics' clinicians started getting errors when opening patient notes. A "cloud hygiene" job had scheduled the KMS key behind the notes for deletion because it looked unused, and during the same clean-up the function's configuration and IAM policy were left pointing at last year's setup. Ticket INC-7702 (in your workspace) explains who uses what. The encrypted notes cannot be re-keyed.
mission.objective: vl-note-reader must open note n-1 end to end (decrypt it and re-encrypt it for the audit archive) using the existing patient-notes key; that key must be usable again and have automatic rotation enabled. The reader's role may use the patient-notes key and must not be able to use the billing key.

mission.name: The Auth Maze
mission.description: Pelican Parcel Lockers' partner API rejects every call, although the published contract says a partner just sends its token in the Authorization header. Partners report three different errors, and a partner who tried signing its requests with SigV4 got further, only to see a 502 from the backend. The partner contract and migration notes are in the escalation file (PX-318) in your workspace.
mission.objective: GET /live/lockers with the correct partner token in the Authorization header must return the locker list with HTTP 200 through the Lambda authorizer and the backend. Requests with no token or a wrong token must still be rejected. Do not switch the authorization off.

mission.name: The Production Incident
mission.description: Black Friday: Northstar Outfitters' storefront tells customers "order received", but nothing has reached the order ledger for 40 minutes. The pipeline is API Gateway, an intake Lambda, an SQS queue, a writer Lambda and a DynamoDB table, and four different people touched four different parts of it this morning. The incident ticket (INC-8830, in your workspace) has the timeline and the rules of engagement.
mission.objective: An order POSTed to /v1/orders on ns-orders-api must be enqueued by the intake function, picked up by the writer function and end up in the ns-orders table, without losing the existing ledger entry o-legacy-1. The intake role may send to ns-order-queue only. Do not rebuild the API or the queue.

mission.name: Leaked Keys
mission.description: A secret scanner found Cinder Games' CI access key in a public repository, still valid after 19 days, and the forensic review shows an attacker used it six days ago and planted a hidden admin user and a role that trusts a foreign account. The pipeline still needs to ship tonight's build. The alert and forensic notes (SEC-INC-0402) are in your workspace.
mission.objective: Respond to the leak: make the leaked key useless, give CI a new working credential in the pipeline's parameter so uploads to cg-build-artifacts continue, remove the attacker's persistence (the hidden user and the foreign role), and shrink cg-build-bot to only what it needs. Do not delete the build user or other staff accounts.

mission.name: Total Recall
mission.description: An intern's clean-up run emptied Marlow & Quayle Legal's case-document bucket and case-index table on a Friday evening. The bucket has (had) versioning and the table has point-in-time recovery, but a storage job also suspended versioning, and one contract had been silently corrupted before the deletion. The incident notes (INC-6611) are in your workspace, with a pointer to the last good moment recorded in SSM.
mission.objective: Bring every document back with its correct content, put every case back into the live ml-case-index table, re-enable versioning on the bucket, and make sure ml-intern can still read and add data but can no longer delete objects, object versions or table items.
